title: Study 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions, Eye-Level Shifts & Pitcher Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
text:
NoteExperiment Registry & Architecture




Experiment ID: EXP-021-PITCH-SEQUENCING-ENTROPY-MARKOV (VALIDATED)
Specification: specs/21_pitch_sequencing_entropy_markov.md | ADR: ADR-017
Full Population: 5,472,291 consecutive regular-season pitch pairs (2015–2025, v_statcast_tunneling)
Chronological Model Split: 2020–2023 Hawk-Eye Train (947,928 paired swings) \(\to\) 2024 Val (281,006) \(\to\) Locked 2025 OOS (279,640)
Companion Work-Along Lab: Lab 21: Pitch Sequencing & Shannon Entropy

title: Study 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions, Eye-Level Shifts & Pitcher Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
Single-pitch physics (EXP-001–EXP-005) evaluates each pitch in isolation, yet hitters update timing and spatial expectations dynamically from pitch to pitch. In EXP-021 (Level 1C), we quantify first-order Markov pitch-group transitions, 2D eye-level vertical × velocity shift surfaces, and count-conditioned Shannon Entropy across 5.47 million regular-season pitch pairs (2015–2025) and isolate pure out-of-sample sequencing value (Seq+) across 279,640 locked 2025 paired swings:

Controlled Sequencing Lift Above Full Pitch Physics & Location: Adding sequencing features (is_repeat_pitch, prev_grp_id, delta_velo_mph, delta_plate_z, delta_plate_x, tunnel_dist_in, post_tunnel_break_in, and strictly prior-season prior_entropy) to a full physics+location+count xgboost hist model (M1) strictly improves locked 2025 OOS Whiff Log-Loss (0.46171 \(\to\) 0.46091), Brier Score (0.14813 \(\to\) 0.14782), and ROC AUC (0.76945 \(\to\) 0.77087, +0.00142 across 279,640 swings).
Shannon Entropy Is a Highly Repeatable Pitcher Trait: Pitcher count-conditioned pitch-mix Shannon Entropy \(H_{\text{count}}\) achieves \(r = 0.8428\) year-over-year stability (2024 -> 2025, n = 398 pitchers), while orthogonal Sequence+ (Seq+) achieves \(r = 0.5936\) (n = 347 pitchers — 3.15x more stable than ERA).
2025 Starting Pitcher Leader: Cy Young ace Tarik Skubal ranks #1 among all MLB starting pitchers (Seq+ = 130.5, 1.965 bits count entropy, 32.9% paired whiff rate across 1,269 paired swings).




First-Order Markov Pitch-Group Transition Matrix

title: Study 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions, Eye-Level Shifts & Pitcher Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
text:
2. Domain Problem & Perceptual-Motor Sequencing Physics

Temporal & Spatial Priming (Gray 2002): A batter’s internal forward model of pitch velocity and arrival height is anchored to the preceding pitch (Pitch N-1). Throwing a high fastball (plate_z ~ 3.2 ft, 96 mph) followed by a low breaking ball (delta_plate_z ~ -1.5 ft, delta_velo ~ -11 mph) exploits both vertical saccade latency and swing-timing error.
Information-Theoretic Predictability: Even elite single-pitch velocity loses deception if a pitcher throws 85% fastballs in 3-1 counts (low Shannon entropy \(H \approx 0.6\) bits). Count-conditioned Shannon entropy \(H(P \mid \text{Count})\) measures how many bits of uncertainty a hitter faces before release.
Why Controlling for Single-Pitch Physics Is Essential: Raw Markov transition tables confound sequencing with pitch type and count (e.g., Breaking -> Breaking shows 35.2% raw whiff rate largely because back-to-back sliders occur heavily in 0-2 / 1-2 two-strike counts). Subtracting M1 (full single-pitch physics + location + count) from M2 isolates pure orthogonal sequencing value (Seq+).

title: Study 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions, Eye-Level Shifts & Pitcher Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Zero-Copy DuckDB Pipeline

Count-Conditioned Shannon Entropy (in Bits): \[H(p, s, c) = -\sum_{t} P(t \mid p, s, c)\,\log_2 P(t \mid p, s, c), \qquad H_{\text{count}}(p, s) = \sum_{c \in 12\text{ counts}} w_{p,s,c}\,H(p, s, c)\]
3D Eye-Level & Velocity Shift Vector: \[\Delta z_i = z_i - z_{i-1}, \qquad \Delta x_{\text{norm}, i} = x_{\text{norm}, i} - x_{\text{norm}, i-1}, \qquad \Delta v_i = v_i - v_{i-1}\]
Orthogonal Pitcher Sequence+ (Seq+, Locked to 2024 Validation Scale): \[\text{Seq+}_{p, s} = 100 + 10 \cdot \frac{\overline{\hat{p}_{\text{M2}} - \hat{p}_{\text{M1}}}_{p,s} - \mu_{2024}}{\sigma_{2024}}\]

-- Exact count-conditioned pitch-mix Shannon Entropy over v_statcast_features
WITH cnt_mix AS (
  SELECT pitcher, game_year AS season, balls, strikes, pitch_type, COUNT(*) AS n_pt
  FROM v_statcast_features
  WHERE game_year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2025 AND game_type = 'R' AND pitch_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
),
cnt_tot AS (
  SELECT pitcher, season, balls, strikes, SUM(n_pt) AS n_cnt FROM cnt_mix GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
),
cnt_ent AS (
  SELECT m.pitcher, m.season, m.balls, m.strikes, t.n_cnt,
         -SUM((m.n_pt::DOUBLE / t.n_cnt) * LOG2(m.n_pt::DOUBLE / t.n_cnt)) AS h_bits
  FROM cnt_mix m JOIN cnt_tot t USING (pitcher, season, balls, strikes)
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
)
SELECT pitcher, season, SUM(n_cnt * h_bits) / SUM(n_cnt) AS count_entropy_bits
FROM cnt_ent GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(n_cnt) >= 250;

title: Study 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions, Eye-Level Shifts & Pitcher Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
text:
7. Downstream Integration & Level 2–5 Applications

Pitch-Design & Game-Planning Diagnostics: Separating Stuff+ (EXP-003), Location+ (EXP-005), ivb_above_slot (EXP-011), and Seq+ (EXP-021) lets pitching coaches identify high-stuff arms leaving whiffs on the table via predictable count patterns (low H_count) or suboptimal eye-level transitions.
Next-Season K% & Strikeout Prop Priors (EXP-004 / EXP-020): Because H_count (\(r = 0.843\)) and Seq+ (\(r = 0.594\)) are highly stable year-over-year and orthogonal to raw pitch aerodynamics, both are prime candidates for Level 2 residual projection features and Level 5 K-Prop pricing.

title: Unsupervised Pitch Clustering with K-Means
text:
In Major League Baseball, pitch types are traditionally labeled by human operators or proprietary MLBAM heuristic algorithms (e.g., Four-Seam Fastball FF, Slider SL, Changeup CH, Curveball CU). However, pitch design exists on a continuous physical continuum: hybrid pitches like “sweepers”, “hard cutters”, and “slurves” often defy discrete classification.
In this analysis, we use unsupervised clustering (K-Means) over raw Statcast flight physics to discover natural pitch movement profiles directly from empirical data.

title: Unsupervised Pitch Clustering with K-Means
text:
In Major League Baseball, pitch types are traditionally labeled by human operators or proprietary MLBAM heuristic algorithms (e.g., Four-Seam Fastball FF, Slider SL, Changeup CH, Curveball CU). However, pitch design exists on a continuous physical continuum: hybrid pitches like “sweepers”, “hard cutters”, and “slurves” often defy discrete classification.
In this analysis, we use unsupervised clustering (K-Means) over raw Statcast flight physics to discover natural pitch movement profiles directly from empirical data.

title: Unsupervised Pitch Clustering with K-Means
text:
Data Extraction via DuckDB
We pull a clean sample of pitches from the mlbr data lake, extracting: - release_speed: Velocity at release point (mph) - pfx_x: Horizontal break induced by Magnus force (converted to inches: pfx_x * 12) - pfx_z: Induced vertical break (inches: pfx_z * 12) - release_spin_rate: Spin rate (rpm)


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  .libPaths(c("/mnt/storage/R/library", .libPaths()))
  library(mlbr)
  library(duckdb)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tidyr)
  library(scales)
})

# Connect to zero-copy DuckDB lake
con <- lake_duckdb()

# Sample 40,000 right-handed pitches with complete tracking metrics
pitches_raw <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT 
    pitch_type,
    player_name,
    p_throws,
    release_speed,
    release_spin_rate,
    pfx_x * 12.0 AS pfx_x_in,
    pfx_z * 12.0 AS pfx_z_in
  FROM statcast
  WHERE p_throws = 'R'
    AND release_speed IS NOT NULL
    AND release_spin_rate IS NOT NULL
    AND pfx_x IS NOT NULL
    AND pfx_z IS NOT NULL
    AND pitch_type IN ('FF', 'FT', 'SI', 'SL', 'CH', 'CU', 'FC')
  USING SAMPLE 40000 (reservoir);
")

cat(sprintf("Retrieved %d pitches for unsupervised clustering.\n", nrow(pitches_raw)))


Retrieved 6605 pitches for unsupervised clustering.

title: Unsupervised Pitch Clustering with K-Means
text:
Feature Scaling & Optimal \(k\) Selection
Because release speed (~90 mph) and spin rate (~2200 rpm) have much larger numerical scales than break measurements (~10 inches), we standardize features using Z-score scaling (\(z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}\)).
We then evaluate within-cluster sum of squares (WSS) across \(k \in \{2, \dots, 8\}\) using the Elbow Method:


Code
# Standardize features
features <- pitches_raw %>%
  select(release_speed, release_spin_rate, pfx_x_in, pfx_z_in) %>%
  scale()

# Compute total within-cluster sum of squares
set.seed(42)
k_values <- 2:8
wss <- numeric(length(k_values))

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {
  km_fit <- kmeans(features, centers = k_values[i], nstart = 10, iter.max = 50)
  wss[i] <- km_fit$tot.withinss
}

elbow_df <- data.frame(k = k_values, wss = wss)

ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2b5c8f", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#f37626", size = 3.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "K-Means Elbow Method for Optimal Pitch Clusters",
    subtitle = "Distinct inflection point observed around k = 4 (Fastballs, Breaking Balls, Offspeed, Cutters)",
    x = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y = "Total Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WSS)"
  )

title: Unsupervised Pitch Clustering with K-Means
text:
Fitting K-Means (\(k = 4\))
We fit our final model with \(k = 4\) clusters, representing the 4 primary pitch movement archetypes:


Code
set.seed(42)
km_final <- kmeans(features, centers = 4, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
pitches_raw$cluster <- as.factor(km_final$cluster)

# Calculate cluster profile means
cluster_profiles <- pitches_raw %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarize(
    count = n(),
    avg_velocity = mean(release_speed),
    avg_spin = mean(release_spin_rate),
    avg_hbreak = mean(pfx_x_in),
    avg_vbreak = mean(pfx_z_in)
  )

knitr::kable(
  cluster_profiles,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Cluster", "Count", "Avg Velo (mph)", "Avg Spin (rpm)", "Avg H-Break (in)", "Avg V-Break (in)")
)

1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
In Study 10, mlbr completes the 5-tier hierarchical sabermetric architecture (Level 1 Pitch Physics \(\rightarrow\) Level 2 True-Talent Projections \(\rightarrow\) Level 3 Team BaseRuns & Standings \(\rightarrow\) Level 4 Markov Game Simulator \(\rightarrow\) Level 5 Market Valuation & Bankroll Optimization). Calibrating a strictly chronological fair-value blend on the 2024 regular season (n = 2,429) and evaluating strictly out-of-sample on the locked 2025 regular season (n = 2,430), plus auditing live archived Polymarket and Kalshi orderbooks:








Pillar
Validated Out-of-Sample Result
Quantitative Finance Implication




Chronological Level 4 Fair Blend (M5)
Fit strictly on 2024 (w_M3 = 0.453, w_M4 = 0.547); achieves textbook Cal Slope = 1.043, AUC = 0.5759, Brier = 0.24354 on locked 2025 OOS (n = 2,430).
Combines starter-level FIP sharpness (M3) with 24 base-out Markov park/bullpen physics (M4) while eliminating both under-confidence (B2: 1.323) and over-confidence (M4: 0.883).


Fractional Kelly vs. Full Kelly (2025 OOS, -105 Vig, EV >= +2%)
Eighth-Kelly (c = 0.125) achieves +2.07% ROI, 131.9u bankroll, Sharpe = 0.91, Max DD = 29.5% vs. Full Kelly (c = 1.0) +0.88% ROI, Max DD = 78.4% (n = 1,325 bets).
Fractional Kelly cuts catastrophic peak-to-trough drawdown by more than half (78.4% \(\rightarrow\) 29.5%) while delivering more than \(2\times\) higher dollar-weighted ROI%.


Execution Friction (-105 Sportsbook vs. -102 Exchange)
Reducing vig from -105/-105 (2.44% overround / 2.38% hold) to -102/-102 (0.99% overround / 0.98% hold) lifts Quarter_Kelly 2025 OOS bankroll from 152.9u (Sharpe 0.93) to 242.0u (Sharpe 1.43).
In low-margin baseball markets, execution venue fee structure is as impactful as model Brier improvements.


Live Archived Prediction Market Microstructure
Cross-season microstructure audit of polymarket-2026-11.parquet (30 2027 MLB WS contracts, \$538.7k liquidity): raw sum of mids = 191.7% (+91.7% overround, 7.0¢ median spread); kalshi-2026-11.parquet (116 contracts, 8.0¢ median spread).
Early offseason prediction-market orderbooks carry massive structural overround; disciplined vig-stripping and spread-aware EV filtering are mandatory before allocating capital.

title: Study 10: Level 5 Market Edge, Closing Line Value (CLV), Fractional Kelly & Prediction Market Valuation
text:
2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Market Mechanics
Converting well-calibrated win probabilities into long-run capital growth requires solving three linked quantitative finance problems:

Expected Value (EV) Net of Market Vig: For a binary market with decimal odds \(O = 1 / q_{\text{ask}}\) (or prediction-market ask price \(q_{\text{ask}}\) in dollars per \$1 payout) and calibrated model probability \(p\): \[\text{EV} = p \cdot (O - 1) - (1 - p) = p \cdot O - 1 = \frac{p - q_{\text{ask}}}{q_{\text{ask}}}\]
Fractional Kelly Criterion Sizing with Simultaneous-Slate Risk Caps: Because MLB slates feature up to 15 simultaneous games per day, all bets on date \(t\) are sized off start-of-day bankroll \(W_t\) (strictly zero intraday look-ahead) with a single-game cap \(f_{\max} = 5\%\) and a daily slate exposure cap of \(35\%\): \[f^* = \min\!\left(0.05,\; c \cdot \max\!\left(0,\; \frac{p \cdot b - (1 - p)}{b}\right)\right), \quad b = O - 1, \quad c \in \{1.0, 0.25, 0.125\}\]
Closing Line Value (CLV) & Multi-Outcome Overround: \[\text{CLV} = \frac{O_{\text{entry}}}{O_{\text{close}}} - 1, \qquad \nu_{\text{futures}} = \sum_{i=1}^{30} q_i^{\text{mid}} - 1\]

title: Study 10: Level 5 Market Edge, Closing Line Value (CLV), Fractional Kelly & Prediction Market Valuation

Strictly Out-of-Sample Game Split: The Level 4 fair-value blend weight (w_M3 = 0.453, w_M4 = 0.547) is estimated strictly via Log-Loss minimization on the 2024 regular season (n = 2,429) and held frozen on the locked 2025 regular season (n = 2,430).
Transparent Benchmark Disclosure: Because historical closing sportsbook odds feeds are not yet ingested in Bronze, the 4,859-game historical backtest benchmarks our Level 4 starter/park/Markov model (M5_L5_Fair_Blend) against the vig-adjusted B2_PriorYr_Pythag_Log5 consensus prior (-105/-105 2.38% vig and -102/-102 1.00% exchange fee) with a synthetic 50% information-absorption closing line (\(q_{\text{close}} = 0.5 q_{\text{open}} + 0.5 p_{\text{fair}}\)). Real-world live market friction is audited directly in Section 5 using archived Polymarket (polymarket-2026-11.parquet) and Kalshi (kalshi-2026-11.parquet) orderbooks.

section: 7. Downstream Integration, Market Applications & Risk Controls
text:
7. Downstream Integration, Market Applications & Risk Controls

Default to Eighth-Kelly (c = 0.125) or Quarter-Kelly (c = 0.25) with Slate Caps: Full Kelly produces untenable 78.4% drawdowns under realistic MLB variance and estimation error. Capping single-game stakes at 5% and total daily slate exposure at 35% prevents correlated single-day ruin.
Enforce Fee-Adjusted EV Thresholds (EV >= +3% on Sportsbooks, >= +2% on Exchanges): On -102 exchanges, EV >= +3% delivers +4.74% Flat ROI (Sharpe 1.79, Max DD 13.6%) and +3.44% Eighth-Kelly ROI (Sharpe 1.49, Max DD 29.0%), whereas on -105 books EV >= +2% balances volume (n = 1,325) with +3.53% Flat / +2.07% Eighth-Kelly ROI.
Never Cross Wide Offseason Spreads on Prediction Markets: With +91.7% structural overround and 7–8¢ median bid-ask spreads in archived Polymarket/Kalshi offseason books, passive limit-order quoting (maker liquidity) rather than market-order crossing is essential to realize positive EV.

title: Study 19: Joint Ordered/Multinomial Total Bases Ladder & Exponential Half-Life State-Space Decay
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
In EXP-019, we execute two targeted mathematical upgrades to mlbr’s Level 5 player-prop pricing stack (EXP-016 and EXP-017) and validate both strictly out-of-sample on locked 2025:

Joint Multinomial Softmax Total Bases Ladder (0, 1, 2, 3, 4+ TB, n = 43,740 OOS): Replacing separate binary logits with a joint 5-class model (nnet::multinom vs. MASS::polr) guarantees zero monotonicity violations (0 / 43,740) across all four retail sportsbook Total Bases rungs (\(P(\text{TB}\ge 1) \ge P(\text{TB}\ge 2) \ge P(\text{TB}\ge 3) \ge P(\text{TB}\ge 4)\)). Relaxing proportional odds via Multinomial Softmax strictly outperforms Ordered Logit (POLR) on 5-class Log-Loss (1.43881 vs 1.44285), Ranked Probability Score (0.18645 vs 0.18672), and power-tail TB >= 4 ROC AUC (0.6003 vs 0.5884, +0.0119 AUC lift).
Exponential Half-Life State-Space Decay (n = 4,859 OOS SP Starts): Replacing EXP-016’s discontinuous flat 30-day boxcar window with a continuous 90-day exponential decay kernel (\(w(\Delta t) = 2^{-\Delta t / H}\), strictly d < t) reveals a clean signal-to-noise curve: a 7-day half-life overreacts to 1-start noise (AUC 0.6761 < 0.6779 flat 30d), 14-day beats flat 30d (AUC 0.6800), and the 2024-selected optimal 30-day half-life (\(H^* = 30\text{d}\), zero 2025 peeking) achieves our strongest K-Prop pricing to date: Count NLL 2.23027 (vs 2.23273), RMSE 2.3002 (vs 2.3068), Over 5.5 K AUC 0.6827 (vs 0.6779), and Over 7.5 K tail Brier 0.11290 (vs 0.11333). (Note: H* = 30d lies at the upper boundary of the tested {7, 14, 21, 30} grid, motivating a future H = 45–60d / season-to-date sweep.)




Ordered Logit vs Multinomial Softmax Total Bases Ladder Ablation

title: Study 19: Joint Ordered/Multinomial Total Bases Ladder & Exponential Half-Life State-Space Decay
text:
2. Domain Problem & Structural Physics

Why Proportional Odds Fails in the Baseball Power Tail: A single (TB = 1) is driven primarily by contact rate, BABIP, and batting-order PA volume, whereas a 4+ TB game (home run or multi-XBH outbreak) is driven disproportionately by Hawk-Eye Bat Speed, Blast Rate, Handedness Park HR Factors (pf_hr_hand), and outfield wind carry. Proportional odds (MASS::polr) constrains every covariate to shift all 4 cumulative thresholds by the same scalar \(\beta_j\). Multinomial Softmax (nnet::multinom) frees each discrete TB class to weight power vs. contact physics distinctly while preserving exact \(\sum_{k=0}^4 p_k = 1\) coherence.
Why a 30-Day Exponential Half-Life Beats Both a Flat 30-Day Boxcar and a 7-Day Window: Starting pitchers pitch only once every 5 days (~6 starts per 30 days). A flat 30-day boxcar treats Day 29 identically to Day 5 and abruptly discards Day 31. An exponential half-life \(H = 30\text{d}\) over a 90-day lookback smoothly retains prior-month talent memory while giving 2x weight to recent starts and avoiding the high variance of a 1-to-2-start 7-day window.
crumbs: Study 19: Joint TB Ladder & Exp-Decay State-Space

title: Study 19: Joint Ordered/Multinomial Total Bases Ladder & Exponential Half-Life State-Space Decay
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Zero-Copy DuckDB Pipeline

Joint Multinomial Total Bases Ladder: \[P(Y_i = k \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = \frac{\exp(\boldsymbol{\gamma}_k^\top \mathbf{x}_i)}{\sum_{m=0}^4 \exp(\boldsymbol{\gamma}_m^\top \mathbf{x}_i)}, \qquad P(\text{TB}_i \ge r \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = \sum_{k=r}^{4} P(Y_i = k \mid \mathbf{x}_i)\]
Ranked Probability Score (RPS): \[\text{RPS} = \frac{1}{4N}\sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{k=0}^3 \Big(\hat{F}_i(k) - \mathbb{I}(y_i \le k)\Big)^2\]
Strictly Causal Exponential Half-Life Kernel (d.gdate < s.gdate): \[w(\Delta t; H) = 2^{-\Delta t / H}, \qquad \text{CSW}_H(p, t) = \frac{\sum w_i\,\text{CSW}_i + 150 \cdot 0.290}{\sum w_i\,P_i + 150}\]

-- Strictly pre-game (d.gdate < s.gdate) exponential half-life decay over v_statcast_features
SELECT s.game_id, s.sp_mlbam,
       (SUM(EXP(-LN(2.0) * DATEDIFF('day', d.gdate, s.gdate) / 30.0) * d.n_csw) + 150.0 * 0.290) /
       (SUM(EXP(-LN(2.0) * DATEDIFF('day', d.gdate, s.gdate) / 30.0) * d.n_pitches) + 150.0) AS csw_h30
FROM starts s
LEFT JOIN daily_pit d
  ON s.sp_mlbam = d.sp_mlbam AND d.gdate < s.gdate AND DATEDIFF('day', d.gdate, s.gdate) BETWEEN 1 AND 90
GROUP BY s.game_id, s.sp_mlbam;

2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Aerodynamics / Officiating Mechanics
Warm air is less dense (\(\rho \propto 1 / T\)), reducing aerodynamic drag on batted balls so fly balls carry 3–4 ft farther per +10°F. Simultaneously, outfield-blowing wind adds tail-wind lift while infield wind suppresses deep fly balls into outs. At the plate, border-pitch strike calls are jointly determined by home-plate umpire zone habits (BASE4_UMP_ID) and catcher receiving mechanics (fielder_2), making environmental and officiating adjustments essential for Totals, F5, and Strikeout Props.

Multi-Category Log5 + Park Factors: \[P_{ij}(E) = \frac{\big(P_{\text{bat}}(E) \cdot P_{\text{pit}}(E) / P_{\text{lg}}(E)\big) \cdot \text{PF}(E)}{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{E}} \big(P_{\text{bat}}(E_k) \cdot P_{\text{pit}}(E_k) / P_{\text{lg}}(E_k)\big) \cdot \text{PF}(E_k)}\]

title: Study 03: Commit-Point Pitch Tunneling & Platoon-Conditioned Stuff+ / Pitching+
text:
2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Physics

2.1 Perceptual Commit-Point Mechanics (Pavlidis & Judge, 2017)
A 95 mph fastball travels from release (~54.5 ft) to home plate (1.417 ft) in roughly 390 ms. Because human visual processing requires ~150 ms and bat swing initiation/execution requires another ~150 ms, hitters must commit to swinging when the ball is roughly 167 ms from home plate — corresponding spatially to the commit plane at \(y_{\text{commit}} = 23.8\text{ ft}\).
Pitch deception operates in two consecutive spatial stages: 1. Pre-Commit Masking (Small tunnel_dist_in): Pitch \(N\) travels down nearly the identical 3D corridor as Pitch \(N-1\) up to \(y = 23.8\text{ ft}\), preventing early pitch recognition. 2. Post-Commit Divergence (Large post_tunnel_break_in): After the hitter commits to a swing plane, Magnus and seam-shifted wake forces bend Pitch \(N\) away from Pitch \(N-1\)’s trajectory, maximizing Pavlidis & Judge’s Break-to-Tunnel Ratio (post_tunnel_break_in / max(tunnel_dist_in, 1.0)).


2.2 Why Linear Models & Naive Release Shortcuts Fail

Coordinate Frame Trap: Statcast’s 9-parameter constant-acceleration kinematics \((v_{x0}, v_{y0}, v_{z0}, a_x, a_y, a_z)\) are defined strictly at \(y_0 = 50.0\text{ ft}\), whereas (release_pos_x, release_pos_z) are reported at release_pos_y (\(\approx 54.5\text{ ft}\)). Integrating forward from release_pos_x using \(t_{\text{dec}}\) omits ~4.5 ft of flight and introduces a 2.87-inch mean (4.69-inch p95) coordinate error at \(y = 23.8\text{ ft}\).
Non-Linearity of Pitch Value: A glove-side slider is devastating on the outer shadow against a same-hand hitter (0-2 count) but crushed in the heart of the zone against an opposite-hand hitter (2-0 count). Analytical Ridge models average away count × location × platoon interactions (0.028% out-of-sample \(R^2\)), whereas xgboost leaps to 3.777%.
Orthogonal Stuff+ vs. Location+ Decomposition (Sarris, Bay, Grove): Separating physical stuff (Stuff+), pure count-and-zone command (Location+), and combined execution (Pitching+) isolates two independent pitcher skills (r = -0.034): Stuff+ governs Strikeout Rate (K%), while Location+ governs Walk Avoidance (BB%).

title: Study 03: Commit-Point Pitch Tunneling & Platoon-Conditioned Stuff+ / Pitching+
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline

3.1 Exact \(y_0 = 50\text{ ft}\) Commit-Point Reconstruction
Given terminal flight time \(t_p\) from \(y_0 = 50.0\text{ ft}\) to the front edge of home plate (\(y_p = 1.417\text{ ft}\)) and commit-point flight time \(t_{\text{dec}}\) to \(y_{\text{commit}} = 23.8\text{ ft}\):
\[t_p = \frac{-\sqrt{v_{y0}^2 + 2 a_y (1.417 - 50.0)} - v_{y0}}{a_y}, \qquad t_{\text{dec}} = \frac{-\sqrt{v_{y0}^2 + 2 a_y (23.8 - 50.0)} - v_{y0}}{a_y}\]
We reconstruct the exact 3D coordinates at \(y_0 = 50.0\text{ ft}\) from observed (plate_x, plate_z) and integrate forward to \(y_{\text{commit}} = 23.8\text{ ft}\) (empirically verified to close back to observed (release_pos_x, release_pos_z) at release_pos_y within 0.046 in mean error across 100,000 Hawk-Eye pitches):
\[x_{50} = \text{plate\_x} - v_{x0} t_p - \frac{1}{2} a_x t_p^2, \qquad z_{50} = \text{plate\_z} - v_{z0} t_p - \frac{1}{2} a_z t_p^2\]
\[x_{\text{dec}} = x_{50} + v_{x0} t_{\text{dec}} + \frac{1}{2} a_x t_{\text{dec}}^2, \qquad z_{\text{dec}} = z_{50} + v_{z0} t_{\text{dec}} + \frac{1}{2} a_z t_{\text{dec}}^2\]
For consecutive pitches (\(N-1 \to N\)) thrown by the same pitcher (prev_pitcher = pitcher) with zero skipped pitch numbers (prev_pitch_number = pitch_number - 1):
\[d_{\text{tunnel}} = 12 \sqrt{(x_{\text{dec}, N} - x_{\text{dec}, N-1})^2 + (z_{\text{dec}, N} - z_{\text{dec}, N-1})^2}\text{ (in)}\]
\[d_{\text{post}} = 12 \sqrt{\bigl((\text{plate\_x}_N - x_{\text{dec}, N}) - (\text{plate\_x}_{N-1} - x_{\text{dec}, N-1})\bigr)^2 + \bigl((\text{plate\_z}_N - z_{\text{dec}, N}) - (\text{plate\_z}_{N-1} - z_{\text{dec}, N-1})\bigr)^2}\text{ (in)}\]
\[\text{Break-to-Tunnel Ratio (BP)} = \frac{d_{\text{post}}}{\max(d_{\text{tunnel}}, 1.0)}, \qquad \text{Plate-to-Tunnel Ratio} = \frac{d_{\text{plate}}}{\max(d_{\text{tunnel}}, 1.0)}\]


3.2 Silver Materialization (v_statcast_tunneling, ADR-001 Strictly Verified)
Executed across all 19 Statcast seasons (2008–2026, preserving all game types per ADR-002 with game_type exposed for zero-copy filtering) by R/materialize_tunneling.R reading canonical sql/02_pitch_tunneling.sql: - Total consecutive pairs materialized: 10,201,496 (2008-03-28 to 2026-10-28) - Integrity & sensor guards: Requires ay > 1e-6, vy0 < -40, plate_x ∈ [-10, 10], plate_z ∈ [-10, 15], t_flight ∈ [0.15, 1.2], and non-null pitch_type/release_speed/kinematics — yielding bad_rows = 0 and dup_groups = 0 on (game_pk, at_bat_number, pitch_number). - Verified ADR-001 sort order: Single-threaded per-year sorted Parquet writes (ROW_GROUP_SIZE = 100000, ZSTD, Hive game_year) verified across all 19 seasons with 0 pitcher sort inversions, 0 row-group min-max overlaps, and 15.0 ms single-pitcher pruned query latency!


3.3 Leak-Free Fastball Anchors & 2024 Out-of-Sample Plus-Scale Lock
Per-pitcher within-season fastball anchors (FF, SI, FC) use strictly prior regular-season pitches (ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING). Plus-scale calibration locks \((\mu_{2024}, \sigma_{\text{pit}, 2024})\) strictly on 2024 Regular-Season out-of-sample predictions (across pitchers with \(\ge 250\) pitches), leaving 2025–2026 100% untouched:
\[\text{Score+}_{i, m} = 100 + 10 \cdot \frac{\hat{r}_{i, m} - \mu_{2024, m}}{\sigma_{\text{pit}, 2024, m}}\]

title: Study 06: Empirical Multi-Year Regressed Ballpark Factors & Handedness Asymmetry
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
Traditional baseball metrics conflate a player’s underlying talent with the physical environment of the venue (air density, altitude, outfield geometry, foul ground area). In Study 06, we construct mlbr’s Empirical Ballpark Factors Engine, generating 3-year rolling regressed park factors across 24 seasons (2002–2025) for all 30 Major League venues from 62,598 Retrosheet games and 16.2M+ play events.








Pillar
Validated Empirical Result
Sabermetric & Forecasting Implication




Altitude Run Lift (DEN02)
Coors Field exhibits a persistent 122.2 3-year regressed run factor (\(+22.2\%\) scoring lift over neutral), non-regressing across 24 seasons (\(5,183\) ft elevation).
Air density reduction expands batted-ball flight and reduces pitch Magnus movement, requiring persistent elevation baselines.


Small-Sample Shrinkage (\(M = 40\))
Unregressed single-season scoring ratios exhibit extreme variance (e.g. Miami MIA02 raw 127.6 in 2024 regresses to 114.1 with 3-year weighting).
Multi-year empirical Bayes shrinkage pulls small-sample noise toward 100 while preserving true venue signal.


Great American Ball Park (CIN09)
Great American Ball Park commands a 132.7 3-year HR factor, leading MLB in overall home run amplification.
Compact outfield fences elevate both LHB (135.2) and RHB (130.8) home run frequencies symmetrically.


Oracle Park Suppression (SFO03)
Oracle Park suppresses home runs to 79.7 (\(20.3\%\) below neutral) due to heavy marine layer and deep right-center field (\(415\) ft Triples Alley).
Dense sea-level air and geometric dimensions suppress power across both handedness splits.


Yankee Stadium Asymmetry (NYC21)
Yankee Stadium short right-field porch (\(314\) ft) produces a +8.7 index point asymmetry favoring left-handed hitters (122.0 LHB vs. 113.3 RHB).
Handedness-specific park factors are mandatory for accurate platoon projection and batter-pitcher matchup modeling.






Figure 1: 3-Year Regressed Run Park Factor vs. Raw Single-Season Scoring Ratio (2024)

title: Study 06: Empirical Multi-Year Regressed Ballpark Factors & Handedness Asymmetry
text:
2. Domain Problem & Sabermetric Theory
Raw single-season park factors suffer from extreme variance: 1. Sample Size Limitations (\(N \approx 81\) games): An 81-game home schedule represents only ~3,000 plate appearances per team. A hot two-week stretch or an unseasonably windy month can shift a park’s raw run ratio by 15–20 index points. 2. Schedule Imbalance: Teams do not play a uniform sample of opponents on the road; division-heavy schedules bias road run baselines. 3. The Bill James / Tom Tango Solution: - Compute home vs. road scoring ratios for both teams combined to neutralize team quality. - Apply the \(N / (N - 1 + \text{Ratio})\) league symmetry correction for a 30-team league. - Pool 3 consecutive seasons with \(3/2/1\) recency weighting. - Regress toward neutral (100) using empirical shrinkage denominators (\(M = 40\) games for runs, \(M = 1500\) PA for HR).

title: Study 06: Empirical Multi-Year Regressed Ballpark Factors & Handedness Asymmetry
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline
For team \(i\) hosted at venue \(p\) during season \(t\): Let \(R_{\text{home, } p}\) be total runs scored by both teams in home games (\(G_{\text{home}}\)). Let \(R_{\text{road, } i}\) be total runs scored by both teams in road games played by team \(i\) (\(G_{\text{road}}\)).
\[\text{Ratio}_{\text{runs}} = \frac{R_{\text{home, } p} / G_{\text{home}}}{R_{\text{road, } i} / G_{\text{road}}}\]
\[\text{PF}_{\text{raw}} = \frac{30 \cdot \text{Ratio}_{\text{runs}}}{29 + \text{Ratio}_{\text{runs}}} \times 100\]
\[\text{PF}_{\text{reg}} = 100 + \left( \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{2} w_k \cdot \text{PF}_{\text{raw}, t-k} \cdot G_{t-k}}{\sum_{k=0}^{2} w_k \cdot G_{t-k}} - 100 \right) \times \frac{\sum G}{\sum G + M}\]

Across all 24 seasons (2002–2025): - All 720 park-seasons satisfy strict physical validity bounds (\(70 \le \text{PF} \le 145\)). - Year-over-year correlation \(r(\text{PF}_t, \text{PF}_{t+1})\) for continuous venues exceeds 0.81 on runs and 0.86 on home runs. - Altitude exhibits a Spearman rank correlation of \(\rho = +0.68\) with run factor elevation.

1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
Raw single-season baseball statistics (ERA, FIP, wOBA, BABIP) are heavily contaminated by finite-sample variance, park/defense noise, and run-environment drift. In Study 04, we construct mlbr’s Level 2 True-Talent Player Projection Engine, bridging Level 1 Atomic Pitch & Batted-Ball Physics (Studies 01–03) directly into Level 3 Team BaseRuns and Level 4 Monte Carlo Game Simulation.








Pillar

True SP fastball velocity drops -5.12 mph and Batter wOBA drops -97 pts from age 27 to 38 (vs. survivor-biased cross-sectional curves at -2.68 mph and -4 pts). Zero-sum normalization removes +0.168 cohort mean FIP drift; 3/2/1 beats 5/4/3 on 5 of 6 pitching metrics (2016–2025).
Standalone unshrunk Delta-Method B3 trails Tom Tango’s lower-variance damped B2 slope slightly on Track 1, but exposes true biological aging free of survivorship bias and powers Stage-1 M4.


Locked 2024 → 2025 Pitcher OOS (\(N = 445\text{–}459\))
M4_Component_FIP achieves 0.77185 wRMSE (-0.03447 vs. true Tango B2 0.80631, \(p_{\text{beat}} = 0.995\)), beating FanGraphs Stuff+ (0.77397). M4_mlbr_StuffPlus cuts FIP to 0.77412, SIERA to 0.52579 (-0.01417, beating FanGraphs 0.52602), and HR/9 to 0.41054 (-0.02194, \(p_{\text{beat}} = 0.998\)).

M4_Statcast_Physics (xwOBA, Pulled Air%, EV90, Zone-Chase Z-O%) cuts wOBA wRMSE from 0.03215 to 0.03121 (-0.00094, \(r = 0.552\), \(p_{\text{beat}} = 0.995\)), BB% to 0.02043 (\(p = 0.993\)), and ISO to 0.04232. Adding Hawk-Eye Bat Tracking cuts Batter K% further to 0.03691 (\(p = 0.995\)).

Track 4 Full-OOS 2025 → 2026 Statcast & 80% CIs

title: Study 04: Chronological True-Talent Player Projections (Marcel, Delta-Method Aging & Tier 1 Physics)
text:
2. Domain Problem & Sabermetric Theory
Forecasting player talent is fundamentally a signal-to-noise extraction problem governed by four interacting mechanisms:

Finite-Sample Binomial & Contact Variance (Carleton Stabilization): A hitter’s K% reaches 50% true-talent reliability in ~50 PA, whereas BABIP, HR/9, and ERA require 500–900+ exposures. Using a single shrinkage denominator across all statistics under-regresses noisy outcomes and over-regresses fast-stabilizing skills.
Survivorship Bias vs. Zero-Sum League Conservation in Aging: Plotting cross-sectional mean wOBA or FIP by age makes 38-year-olds appear nearly identical to 27-year-olds because only elite outliers remain employed at 38. Conversely, applying uncentered within-player Delta-Method declines directly to a returning MLB cohort shifts the projected league average upward by +0.168 FIP because retiring veterans are replaced by incoming rookies. Tango’s Zero-Sum Conservation Law resolves both: estimate true biological slopes via midpoint harmonic-mean-weighted within-player pairs (with linear tail extrapolation past Age 39 so veteran decline remains strictly monotone), then zero-center the projected cohort’s exposure-weighted aging shift to conserve the T-1 league run environment.
Why xwOBA Alone Is Incomplete (Spray & Swing-Decision Blind Spots): Standard xwOBA depends solely on Exit Velocity and Launch Angle, ignoring horizontal spray angle. Pulled air balls (LA >= 10°, spray < -15° RHB / > +15° LHB — validated against FanGraphs Pull% at r = 0.932 overall and 0.962–0.977 within batter handedness) produce vastly higher wOBA than opposite-field fly balls (r = +0.203 with RHB wOBA - xwOBA — e.g., Isaac Paredes’s 39.1% raw 2025 Pulled Air% / 35.1% 3-year regressed prior drove a .352 observed wOBA over his .314 regressed xwOBA). Likewise, raw O-Swing% rewards overly passive hitters, whereas Zone-Chase Selectivity (Z-Swing% - O-Swing%, a SEAGER-inspired box-zone proxy) directly isolates pitch-recognition aggression (\(r_{\text{YoY}} = 0.800\)).
Preventing Sensor-Tier Over-Shrinkage via Stage-2 Residual Stacking: Newer Hawk-Eye sensors (mlbr Stuff+ OOS from 2024+, Hawk-Eye Bat Tracking from 2023+) have only 1 calibration season vs. 8–9 seasons for core Statcast metrics. Re-estimating 18 collinear predictors from scratch on \(N \approx 450\) pitchers with L2 cross-validation crushes the dynamic range (cal_slope = 1.8–2.2). Holding the multi-year M4_Statcast_Physics forecast fixed as a Stage-1 offset and learning a zero-mean Stage-2 Residual Ridge over the 3–4 orthogonal new sensor features preserves cal_slope ≈ 1.00 while cleanly capturing incremental physical lift.

title: Study 04: Chronological True-Talent Player Projections (Marcel, Delta-Method Aging & Tier 1 Physics)
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline

3.1 Exact Baseball Outs Conversion & July-1 Age Invariants
In v_fangraphs_pitch, IP is stored in baseball outs notation (.1 \(= 1/3\), .2 \(= 2/3\); verified 314–349 rows/season, 0 decimal rows). Every aggregation converts to exact decimal innings prior to sum-before-divide:
\[\text{IP}_{\text{true},i,s} = \lfloor \text{IP}_{i,s} \rfloor + \frac{\text{round}\big(10 \cdot (\text{IP}_{i,s} - \lfloor \text{IP}_{i,s} \rfloor)\big)}{3}, \qquad \text{Age}_{i,s} = s - \text{birth\_year}_i - \mathbb{I}(\text{birth\_month}_i \ge 7)\]
Verified 6,703 / 6,703 (100.00%) exact match between Chadwick birth dates and FanGraphs Age, and 3,687 / 3,687 (100.00%) join parity between v_fangraphs_pitch (TBF >= 50, 2020–2025) and Tier 1 Gold pitcher_stuff_plus.parquet.


3.2 Era-Adjusted Marcel, Midpoint Delta Aging & Component-Reconstructed FIP
For target season \(T\), role \(g \in \{\text{SP}, \text{RP}, \text{BAT}\}\), recency weights \((w_1, w_2, w_3)\) (5/4/3 batters; 3/2/1 pitchers), and pre-backtest (2006–2015) calibrated reliability denominators \(M_r\):
\[\hat{r}^{\text{Marcel}}_{i,T} = \mu_{\text{lg},T-1,g} + \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{3} w_k \, N_{i,T-k} \, (r_{i,T-k} - \mu_{\text{lg},T-k,g})}{\sum_{k=1}^{3} w_k \, N_{i,T-k} + M_r}\]
(2020 COVID-19 60-game season retains raw exposure \(N_{i,2020}\) in rate precision weighting while pro-rating playing-time inputs by \(162/60 = 2.70\times\). Baseline B2_Marcel_LinAge implements Tom Tango’s (2004) exact direct age multiplier \(m(a) = 1 + 0.006(29 - a)\) for \(a \le 29\) and \(1/(1 + 0.003(a - 29))\) for \(a > 29\), followed by Step 6 projected-exposure league rebaselining.)
Consecutive same-player, same-role pairs \((s-1, s)\) with \(s \in [2003, T-1]\) estimate smooth midpoint (age_mid = age - 0.5) harmonic-mean-weighted Delta-Method curves \(\hat{\delta}_g(a)\) with inverse-variance weights \(W_{i,a}^{\text{harm}} = \frac{2 N_{i,s-1} N_{i,s}}{N_{i,s-1} + N_{i,s}}\) and linear marginal-slope extrapolation beyond [21, 39] (preventing endpoint clamping artifacts at Age 40+). Integrating from weighted historical age \(\bar{a}_{i,T}\) to target age \(a_{i,T}\) and applying Tango’s zero-sum normalization yields B3:
\[\Delta^{\text{raw}}_{\text{age}}(i, T) = \int_{\bar{a}_{i,T}}^{a_{i,T}} \hat{\delta}_g(u)\,du, \qquad \Delta^{\text{norm}}_{\text{age}}(i, T) = \Delta^{\text{raw}}_{\text{age}}(i, T) - \frac{\sum_{j \in g} \widehat{N}_{j,T}\,\Delta^{\text{raw}}_{\text{age}}(j, T)}{\sum_{j \in g} \widehat{N}_{j,T}}\]


3.3 Stage-1 Expanding Physics Ridge, Stage-2 Sensor Residual Stacking & Uncertainty Bands

Stage-1 Expanding Statcast Physics (M4_Statcast_Physics): Season-grouped L2 Ridge (glmnet, \(\alpha=0\)) trained strictly on target seasons 2016 .. T-1 (0 imputed cells across all folds) over B3 rates plus regressed Statcast physics (SwStr%, CSW%, FBv, delta_fbv, GB%, HardHit%, Barrel%, xERA, pulled_air_allowed_pct, strictly seasonal pooled sum-before-shrink PVI_xwoba/PVI_csw for pitchers; xwOBA, xwOBA - wOBA, Barrel%, HardHit%, EV90, pulled_air_pct, sweet_spot_pct, O-Swing%, Z-Contact%, SwStr%, zone_chase_selectivity for batters).
Stage-2 Residual Sensor Stack (M4_mlbr_StuffPlus, M4_BatTracking): Holds Stage-1 fixed as an offset and fits a compact zero-mean residual Ridge on 2023 → 2024 (2024 100% unseen by Study 03’s 2015–2023 XGBoost training) over the 3–4 orthogonal new sensor variables (stuff_plus_t1, loc_plus_t1, pitch_plus_t1, tunnel_plus_t1 or batspeed_t1, blast_t1, sq_swing_t1, swing_len_t1).
Component-Reconstructed FIP (M4_Component_FIP): Synthesizes projected K%, BB%, HR/9, regressed HBP%, role TBF/IP, and prior-year \(c\text{FIP}_{T-1}\) into an internally consistent run-prevention forecast.
Exposure-Calibrated 80% Uncertainty Bands: Regressing pre-2025 OOS squared residuals \(e_i^2\) on \(1/N_i\) decomposes uncertainty into irreducible talent variance + exposure noise:

\[\text{CI}_{80\%}(i, T) = \hat{y}_{i,T} \pm 1.2816 \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{skill}}^2 + \frac{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{noise}}^2}{\widehat{N}_{i,T}}}\]

Track 2 (2019–2025, \(N = 2,834\text{–}2,945\) pitchers, \(2,768\) batters): M4_Statcast_Physics decisively beats Pure Marcel at \(p_{\text{beat}} = 1.000\) across Pitcher FIP (0.88757 → 0.85389, \(r: 0.330 \to 0.425\)), SIERA (0.63107 → 0.60763), HR/9 (0.46256 → 0.44953), K% (0.04031 → 0.03968), ERA (1.19749 → 1.15694), Batter wOBA (0.03443 → 0.03361, \(r: 0.505 \to 0.536\)), OBP (0.03171 → 0.03090), BB% (0.02157 → 0.02082), and beats on K% (p = 0.975), SLG (p = 0.940), and ISO (p = 0.915).
Track 4 (2025 → 2026 Regular-Season Statcast, 2,429 games) & Pure-OOS Calibration Sensitivity:

Pitcher K% (\(N = 461\)): Calibrating M4_mlbr_StuffPlus purely on 2024 → 2025 (val_calibration Stuff+) and scoring untouched 2025 → 2026 (test_oos Stuff+) achieves 0.03688 wRMSE (\(r = 0.7006\), \(p = 1.000\)), beating M4_Statcast_Physics (0.03710), B3 (0.03915), and B2 (0.03942).
Pitcher BB% (\(N = 461\), honest negative result): Pure Marcel B2 (0.02060) outperformed M4_Statcast_Physics (0.02099), M4_mlbr_StuffPlus (0.02098), and PureOOSCal (0.02083, \(p = 0.130\)) due to a +0.0046 league walk-rate regime shift in 2026.
Batters (\(N = 411\)): M4_Statcast_Physics slashes 2026 xwOBA wRMSE from 0.02776 to 0.02570 (\(r = 0.6601\), \(p = 1.000\)), BB% from 0.02217 to 0.02119 (\(p = 0.993\)), and K% from 0.03542 to 0.03439 (\(p = 0.983\)).

text:
NoteResearch Standard & Framework Compliance



This study adheres to the Q-CRISP (Quantitative Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining) methodology and the Full-Population Invariant: all mathematical derivations and empirical distributions are evaluated over the entire 14,643,543 pitch population without arbitrary subsampling.

title: Study 01: Aerodynamics, Trajectory Physics & Approach Angles
text:
1. Business & Scientific Understanding

1.1 The Classical Evaluation Deficit
For decades, scouting and public sabermetrics evaluated pitchers primarily through two physical proxies: raw release velocity (\(v_{\text{release}}\)) and raw spin rate (\(\omega\)). While velocity correlates with swinging strike rate, these bulk variables consistently fail to explain why pitchers with identical velocity profiles exhibit vastly divergent whiff rates.
A prime example is the contrasting performance of fastballs with identical 95 mph release speed: - Pitcher A throws a 95 mph four-seamer that generates a 28% swing-and-miss rate. - Pitcher B throws a 95 mph four-seamer that generates a 12% swing-and-miss rate and is heavily punished on contact.
The missing physical mechanism lies in flight trajectory geometry: specifically, the angle at which the projectile traverses the strike zone relative to the batter’s plane of swing, known as the Vertical Approach Angle (VAA) and Horizontal Approach Angle (HAA).


1.2 The 5-Tier Hierarchical Predictive Architecture
Within the mlbr quantitative betting architecture, individual pitch dynamics constitute Level 1 (Pitch Physics & Quality). Level 1 models do not predict game winners directly; rather, they estimate the fundamental run-prevention and swing-inducing quality of every pitch thrown by a pitcher, conditioned on release geometry and trajectory mechanics.
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 5: Betting Market Edge & Kelly Staking (Polymarket / Kalshi)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    ^
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 4: Game Simulation Engine (Monte Carlo Run-Expectancy Markov)      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    ^
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 3: Team BaseRuns & Run-to-Win Translation                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    ^
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 2: Player Projections (PECOTA / ZiPS / Marcel Hierarchical Comps)  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    ^
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 1: Pitch Physics & Quality (Stuff+, Location+, Pitching+)         |
| -> Study 01 establishes the aerodynamic foundations for Level 1         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+


1.3 Hypotheses

Hypothesis 1.1 (Trajectory Independence): Approach angles (VAA/HAA) provide orthogonal predictive information to raw velocity and induced vertical break (IVB).
Hypothesis 1.2 (Height-Conditional Whiff Lift): A four-seam fastball entering the top of the strike zone with a flatter VAA than physically expected for its height (\(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}} > 0\)) produces a non-linear increase in swinging strikes due to batter perceptual motor error.

2. Data Understanding & Lake Verification

2.1 Lake Population & Completeness
The empirical dataset utilized in this study spans the entire modern tracking era from March 25, 2008 to October 28, 2026, preserved in the mlbr canonical data lake at /mnt/storage/Rprojects/mlbr/data/raw/statcast/.

Total Ingested Pitches: 14,643,543
Competitive MLB Games: 52,546
Seasons Covered: 19 (2008–2026)
Tracked 9-Parameter Trajectories: 13,787,464 (94.15% valid trajectory coverage; pre-2015 PITCHf/x and Statcast combined).
Column Ingestion Fidelity: 119 / 119 Statcast fields preserved (0 columns dropped).



2.2 Temporal Validation Partitioning
To guarantee zero look-ahead bias and maintain strict academic reproducibility: - Historical Baseline & Feature Fits: Seasons 2008 through 2023 (\(N = 12,188,235\) pitches). - Out-of-Time Validation Set: Seasons 2024 through 2026 (\(N = 2,455,308\) pitches).

title: Study 01: Aerodynamics, Trajectory Physics & Approach Angles
text:
3. Mathematical Derivation: Aerodynamic Trajectory Features

3.1 Terminal Velocity at the Strike Zone Plane
Statcast tracks the projectile’s trajectory from initial release (\(y_0 = 50.0\) ft from home plate) to the front edge of home plate (\(y_f = 1.417\) ft, or 17 inches) under constant acceleration assumptions: \[\vec{a}(t) = \begin{bmatrix} a_x \\ a_y \\ a_z \end{bmatrix}, \quad \vec{v}_0 = \begin{bmatrix} v_{x0} \\ v_{y0} \\ v_{z0} \end{bmatrix}\]
Using the kinematic equations under constant longitudinal drag \(a_y\): \[v_{yf}^2 = v_{y0}^2 + 2 a_y (y_f - 50.0)\]
Because the baseball moves toward home plate in a negative \(y\)-direction, \(v_{yf}\) is strictly negative: \[v_{yf} = -\sqrt{v_{y0}^2 + 2 a_y (1.417 - 50.0)}\]
The total time of flight \(t_{\text{flight}}\) from the 50-foot tracking point to plate contact is: \[t_{\text{flight}} = \frac{v_{yf} - v_{y0}}{a_y}\]
The terminal horizontal (\(v_{xf}\)) and vertical (\(v_{zf}\)) velocities at plate arrival are: \[v_{xf} = v_{x0} + a_x \cdot t_{\text{flight}}\] \[v_{zf} = v_{z0} + a_z \cdot t_{\text{flight}}\]


3.2 Vertical & Horizontal Approach Angles
The Vertical Approach Angle (VAA) is the angle in degrees between the velocity vector and the horizontal ground plane at the front of home plate: \[\text{VAA} = \text{atan2}(v_{zf}, -v_{yf}) \times \frac{180}{\pi}\]
The Horizontal Approach Angle (HAA) is the lateral approach angle relative to the straight line connecting the mound and home plate: \[\text{HAA} = \text{atan2}(v_{xf}, -v_{yf}) \times \frac{180}{\pi}\]


3.3 Platoon-Normalized Coordinates
Pitch location (plate_x) is defined from the umpire’s perspective (positive = catcher’s right / right-handed batter outside). To model pitch effectiveness invariant to batter handedness, we define Platoon-Normalized Plate X (plate_x_norm): \[\text{plate\_x\_norm} = \text{plate\_x} \times \begin{cases} -1.0 & \text{if batter stands Left (L)} \\ +1.0 & \text{if batter stands Right (R)} \end{cases}\] Under this transformation, positive values always represent pitches away / glove-side from the batter, and negative values represent inside / arm-side pitches.


3.4 Statcast Concentric Attack Zones
Following the MLB Statcast attack zone framework, every pitch is mapped into one of four concentric zones: - Heart: \(|\text{plate\_x}| \le 0.55\) ft and \(\text{plate\_z} \in [1.83, 3.17]\) ft. - Shadow: Edges of the strike zone (\(|\text{plate\_x}| \le 1.11\) ft and \(\text{plate\_z} \in [1.25, 3.75]\) ft), excluding Heart. - Chase: Expanded boundary (\(|\text{plate\_x}| \le 1.66\) ft and \(\text{plate\_z} \in [0.67, 4.33]\) ft), excluding Shadow. - Waste: All pitches completely outside the chase perimeter.


3.5 Expected VAA and VAA Difference (\(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}}\))
Gravity dictates that pitches crossing the plate lower in the zone necessarily have steeper downward trajectories than pitches crossing high. To isolate the pitcher’s aerodynamic creation of flatness from mere location, we fit an empirical baseline for Four-Seam Fastballs: \[\mathbb{E}[\text{VAA} \mid \text{plate\_z}] = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{plate\_z}\]
Empirical Ordinary Least Squares estimation over 1,000,901 modern fastballs yields: \[\mathbb{E}[\text{VAA}] = -7.71^\circ + 1.06 \cdot \text{plate\_z}\]
We then define the critical feature VAA Above Expected: \[\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}} = \text{VAA} - \mathbb{E}[\text{VAA} \mid \text{plate\_z}]\]

section: 5. Signal Evaluation: The Optical Mechanism of Whiff Lift
text:
5. Signal Evaluation: The Optical Mechanism of Whiff Lift

5.1 The “Rising Fastball” Optical Illusion
Human batters do not visually track the ball all the way into the catcher’s mitt. Instead, the batter’s neuromuscular system extrapolates the ball’s final trajectory based on sensory cues acquired during the first 150 milliseconds of flight.
When a pitcher delivers a fastball from a low release height with high backspin (high Induced Vertical Break), the pitch arrives at the top of the zone with \(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}} > +1.5^\circ\) (flatter than expected). To the batter, the pitch appears to “rise” or carry through the hitting zone. The bat path, calibrated to an average descent angle of \(-5.5^\circ\), swings through the plane directly beneath the ball, producing a whiff.



Figure 2: Four-Seam Fastball Whiff Rate vs. VAA Above Expected




5.2 Quantitative Whiff Lift
As demonstrated in Figure 2: - Four-seamers with negative \(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}}\) (steeper than expected, \(\le -1.5^\circ\)) generate whiff rates below 15%. - Neutral fastballs (\(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}} \approx 0.0^\circ\)) generate baseline whiff rates of 21%. - Elite flat fastballs (\(\text{VAA}_{\text{diff}} \ge +2.0^\circ\)) produce whiff rates exceeding 32% on swings—a +52% relative increase in swing-and-miss efficiency without requiring additional velocity.

text:
2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Grounding
Public baseball forecasting evolved through five distinct intellectual eras: 1. Marcel (Tom Tango, 2004): 3-year weighted baseline (5/4/3) + universal reliability regression + piecewise-linear age adjustment. 2. ZiPS (Dan Szymborski): 4-year weighted baseline (8/5/4/3) + position/archetype aging curves + multi-year career horizon forecasts. 3. PECOTA (Nate Silver, 2003): Non-parametric nearest-neighbor (\(k\)-NN) similarity scores across decades of baseball history, outputting full 10th–90th percentile distributions, breakout/collapse probabilities, and attrition/survival rates. 4. THE BAT / OOPSY (Derek Carty / Jordan Rosenblum): Incorporating Statcast batted-ball physics (xwOBA, EV90, Pulled Air%) and pitch tracking (Stuff+, Location+). 5. ATC / Depth Charts Consensus: Ensembling multiple orthogonal projection systems via out-of-sample inverse-variance / convex stacking.

title: Study 07: PECOTA k-NN Similarity Comps, ZiPS Archetype Multi-Year Aging & Non-Pitch Defense/Baserunning EDA
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline

3.1 Era-Neutralized Historical \(z\)-Scores (1960–2025)
To compare a 1963 Mickey Mantle or 1996 Gary Sheffield directly against a 2025 hitter without run-environment distortion, every feature is standardized within its own season \(s\) and role \(g\): \[z_{i,s}^{(f)} = \frac{x_{i,s}^{(f)} - \mu_{s,g}^{(f)}}{\sigma_{s,g}^{(f)}}\]


3.2 Vectorized PECOTA \(k\)-NN Kernel & Strict Anti-Leakage Guard
For any target season \(T\), candidate historical comps must satisfy \(s \le T - 2\) so their subsequent \(s+1\) outcome is strictly \(\le T - 1\). Pairwise weighted Euclidean distances \(d_{ij}\) across all 70,967 historical seasons are computed in milliseconds via BLAS matrix algebra (\(\|x - y\|^2 = \|x\|^2 + \|y\|^2 - 2xy^\top\)) and weighted by a Gaussian kernel \(w_j = \exp(-\frac{1}{2}(d_{ij}/\tau)^2)\) over the top \(k = 50\) nearest neighbors.

title: Study 20: Interior Half-Life Sweep, Dynamic In-Season Starter Workload (BF/GS) & Multivariate Copula-Kelly Staking
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
In EXP-020, we resolve two structural gaps surfaced during our independent audits of EXP-018 and EXP-019:

Interior Half-Life Optimum (H = 60d OOS) & Dynamic In-Season Starter Workload (BF/GS, n = 4,859 Locked 2025 Starts):

Expanding the strictly pre-game (d < t) exponential decay sweep from {14..30d} to {14, 30, 45, 60, 90, 180d} reveals an interior OOS optimum around H = 60d (Count NLL 2.22972, O5.5 K AUC 0.6834, plateauing smoothly through 180d).
Adding strictly causal exponentially-decayed in-season starter workload (bf_gs_h60, EB-shrunk \(M = 4\) starts toward prior eb_bf_gs) delivers a major step-change across every metric: NegBin dispersion \(\hat{\theta}\) jumps from 51.78 \(\to\) 84.32 (explaining ~40% of remaining strikeout overdispersion!), locked 2025 Count NLL drops 2.23014 \(\to\) 2.22598, Strikeout RMSE falls 2.2999 \(\to\) 2.2899, Over 5.5 K ROC AUC reaches 0.6849, and Over 7.5 K tail Brier improves 0.11288 \(\to\) 0.11249.

Multivariate Copula-Kelly Portfolio Staking (n = 2,430 Locked 2025 Games, 3 Simultaneous Markets):

Integrating EXP-018’s 2024-trained Gaussian Copula correlation matrix (\(\hat{\rho}(\text{ML, HSP K}) = +0.192\), \(\hat{\rho}(\text{HSP K, Over 8.5}) = -0.182\)) into an exact box-constrained Quadratic Program (max f'mu - (1/(2c)) f'Sigma f) automatically applies a -7.98% stake haircut across 811 positively correlated multi-leg games and a +11.64% stake boost across 651 negatively correlated natural hedges, reducing daily portfolio volatility (7.48% \(\to\) 7.41%) under a transparent -105 synthetic prior-baseline book benchmark (explicitly disclosed per ADR-009).





Interior Half-Life Sweep and Dynamic BF/GS Workload Lift

title: Study 20: Interior Half-Life Sweep, Dynamic In-Season Starter Workload (BF/GS) & Multivariate Copula-Kelly Staking
text:
2. Domain Problem & Quantitative Mechanics

Why Starter Workload (BF/GS) Drives Strikeout Overdispersion: Expected strikeouts factor into \(E[\text{SO}] = \text{K\%} \times \text{BF/GS}\). In EXP-016 and EXP-019, we dynamically updated in-season CSW% and K%, but held eb_bf_gs frozen at season - 1. In reality, starters returning from injury (IL pitch-count ramps), stretched-out former relievers, and short-leash rookies exhibit persistent in-season BF/GS regimes. Modeling causal trailing BF/GS directly from prior starts (p.gdate < s.gdate, zero reliever contamination) explains a massive share of extra-Poisson count variance (\(\hat{\theta}: 51.8 \to 84.3\)).
Why Independent Kelly Misallocates Multi-Market Same-Game Slates: Betting Home ML and Home SP Over 5.5 K in the same game concentrates shared variance (\(\Sigma_{12} > 0\)), whereas betting Home SP Over 5.5 K alongside Game Over 8.5 forms a partial hedge (\(\Sigma_{23} < 0\)). Second-order Multivariate Kelly adjusts each ticket’s stake analytically via \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\mu}\).

title: Study 20: Interior Half-Life Sweep, Dynamic In-Season Starter Workload (BF/GS) & Multivariate Copula-Kelly Staking
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Zero-Copy DuckDB Pipeline

Causal Starter Workload (BF/GS) State-Space (M_GS = 4 starts): \[\text{BF\_GS}_H(p, t) = \frac{\sum_{d < t,\, s(d)=s(t)} 2^{-(t-d)/H}\,\text{BF}_{p,d} + 4.0 \cdot \text{eb\_bf\_gs}_{p, s-1}}{\sum_{d < t,\, s(d)=s(t)} 2^{-(t-d)/H} + 4.0}\]
Exact Copula-Covariance Multivariate Kelly QP (f in [0, 0.05]^m, 35% daily slate cap): \[\max_{\mathbf{f} \in [0, 0.05]^m} \; \mathbf{f}^\top \boldsymbol{\mu} - \frac{1}{2c} \mathbf{f}^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \mathbf{f}, \qquad \Sigma_{jk} = O_j O_k \Big(C_{\text{Gauss}}(p_j, p_k; s_j s_k \hat{\rho}_{jk, 2024}) - p_j p_k\Big)\]

-- Strictly causal in-season starter workload (BF/GS) from prior starts only
SELECT s.game_id, s.sp_mlbam,
       (COALESCE(SUM(EXP(-LN(2.0) * DATEDIFF('day', p.gdate, s.gdate) / 60.0) * p.sp_bf), 0) + 4.0 * s.eb_bf_gs) /
       (COALESCE(SUM(EXP(-LN(2.0) * DATEDIFF('day', p.gdate, s.gdate) / 60.0)), 0) + 4.0) AS bf_gs_h60
FROM starts s
LEFT JOIN starts p
  ON s.sp_mlbam = p.sp_mlbam AND s.season = p.season
  AND p.gdate < s.gdate AND DATEDIFF('day', p.gdate, s.gdate) BETWEEN 1 AND 180
GROUP BY s.game_id, s.sp_mlbam, s.eb_bf_gs;

6. Correlation-Regime Case Studies & Honest Trade-Off Disclosure

Positively Correlated Tickets (n = 811 games, -7.98% haircut): When mlbr flags both Home ML and Home SP Over 5.5 K as +EV in the same contest (\(\hat{\rho} = +0.192\)), the QP automatically trims combined stake to avoid double-counting shared starter dominance variance.
Negatively Correlated Hedges (n = 651 games, +11.64% boost): When Home SP Over 5.5 K and Game Over 8.5 are both +EV (\(\hat{\rho} = -0.182\)), off-diagonal covariance is negative, allowing larger combined allocation at the same variance budget.
Synthetic Benchmark Disclosure (ADR-009): Realized ROI (~12.9%) and Sharpe (~7.9) reflect pricing against a naive prior-season baseline book (p_b2, exp_so_m1, exp_total_runs + 2.38% vig) rather than sharp live closing odds. Real-world edge against Pinnacle/Circa will be materially smaller; the true takeaway is the relative variance compression (7.48% \(\to\) 7.41%) and disciplined correlation-aware sizing.

Two structural realities govern sharp in-season MLB pricing: (1) starter strikeout counts are overdispersed (Var/Mean = 1.28) because managers pull struggling starters after 3–4 innings while riding dominant aces through 7+, and (2) pitcher true talent is non-stationary within a season due to pitch-mix changes, fatigue, and minor injuries — making a fast-stabilizing process sensor like trailing 30-day CSW% (M = 150 pitches) far superior to static preseason priors alone.

title: Lab 02 Work-Along: 4-Quadrant Platoon Physics, Break Symmetry & PVI
text:
1. Batter-Perspective Break Symmetry (hb_away_in) & PVI Math
Statcast measures horizontal break (pfx_x) from the catcher’s point of view (+ toward 1st base, - toward 3rd base). To compare all four handedness matchups (RvR, RvL, LvL, LvR) on a single physical axis, we define batter-perspective horizontal break away from the hitter:
\[\text{hb\_away\_in} = \begin{cases} +12 \cdot \text{pfx\_x} & \text{if } \text{stand} = \text{R} \text{ (1st-base side is away)} \\ -12 \cdot \text{pfx\_x} & \text{if } \text{stand} = \text{L} \text{ (3rd-base side is away)} \end{cases}\]
Under this coordinate transform, a 15-inch sweeper yields +15.0 in (breaking away from the barrel) in both RvR and LvL, and -15.0 in (breaking back into the barrel) in both RvL and LvR.

Empirical Bayes Pitcher Platoon Vulnerability Index (PVI)
Raw same-hand vs. opposite-hand splits are noisy for relievers and rookies. We stabilize each pitcher’s platoon split using the harmonic-mean effective sample size \(n_{\text{eff}}\) and shrinkage constant \(M = 800\) pitches:
\[n_{\text{eff}} = \frac{2 \, n_{\text{same}} \, n_{\text{opp}}}{n_{\text{same}} + n_{\text{opp}}}, \qquad \text{PVI}_{\text{xwOBA}} = \frac{n_{\text{eff}}}{n_{\text{eff}} + 800} \cdot (\text{xwOBA}_{\text{opp}} - \text{xwOBA}_{\text{same}})\]

A small sample (120 same vs. 120 opp, raw +0.080 split) receives only 13.0% weight → PVI = +0.010.
A large sample (1,800 same vs. 1,800 opp, raw +0.080 split) receives 69.2% weight → PVI = +0.055.

text:
Full Runnable Script (workbooks/lab19_ordered_tb_exp_decay_statespace_workbook.R)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# ==============================================================================
# Lab 19: Joint Ordered/Multinomial Total Bases Ladder & Exponential Decay
# Companion Work-Along Workbook for Study 19 (EXP-019)
# ==============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(mlbr); library(DBI); library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
})

cat("=== Lab 19: Joint TB Ladder & Exponential Half-Life State-Space ===\n")
lake <- mlbr::default_lake()
con  <- mlbr::lake_duckdb(lake)
on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), add = TRUE)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET memory_limit = '12GB';")

# PART 1: First-Principles Exponential Decay Kernel vs Flat 30-Day Boxcar
days_ago <- 1:60
w_flat30 <- ifelse(days_ago <= 30, 1.0, 0.0)
w_exp14  <- 2^(-days_ago / 14)
w_exp30  <- 2^(-days_ago / 30)
cat(sprintf("Day 5 vs Day 29 weight ratio — Flat30: %.2fx | Exp14: %.2fx | Exp30: %.2fx\n",
            w_flat30[5]/w_flat30[29], w_exp14[5]/w_exp14[29], w_exp30[5]/w_exp30[29]))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 1:
# Verify why w_exp30 retains smooth memory past Day 30 while giving 2x weight to recent starts.
stopifnot(abs(w_exp30[30] - 0.5) < 1e-12 && w_exp30[45] > 0 && w_flat30[31] == 0)
cat("CHECKPOINT 1 PASS: Exponential half-life decay kernel verified.\n")

# PART 2: Zero-Copy DuckDB SQL Monotonicity & Ladder Verification on Locked 2025
p_tb <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/ordered_tb_ladder_backtest_2024_2025.parquet")
tb_chk <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf("
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS n_starts_2025,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p_mn_ge1 < p_mn_ge2 OR p_mn_ge2 < p_mn_ge3 OR p_mn_ge3 < p_mn_ge4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_violations,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_mn_ge1), 2) AS avg_p_ge1,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_mn_ge2), 2) AS avg_p_ge2,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_mn_ge3), 2) AS avg_p_ge3,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_mn_ge4), 2) AS avg_p_ge4
  FROM read_parquet('%s')
", p_tb))
print(tb_chk)

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 2:
# Confirm n_violations == 0 across all 43,740 locked 2025 batter-games.
stopifnot(tb_chk$n_violations == 0L && tb_chk$n_starts_2025 == 43740L)
cat("CHECKPOINT 2 PASS: Zero monotonicity violations across all 43,740 OOS batter-games.\n")

# PART 3: Dark Cyber Diagnostic Chart — Half-Life Curve on Locked 2025 OOS Over 5.5 K AUC
p_dk <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/exp_decay_kprop_ablation_2025.parquet")
dk_df <- arrow::read_parquet(p_dk)
flat_auc <- dk_df$oos_2025_auc_o55[dk_df$model == "M4_EXP016_Flat30d"]

p_lab19 <- ggplot(dk_df |> filter(!is.na(half_life_days)), aes(x = half_life_days, y = oos_2025_auc_o55)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = flat_auc, color = "#f43f5e", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(color = "#38bdf8", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#10b981", size = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(7, 14, 21, 30)) +
  labs(
    title = "Lab 19 Diagnostic: Exponential Half-Life vs. Flat 30d Boxcar (Over 5.5 K AUC)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Red dashed = EXP-016 Flat 30d (%.4f) | H*=30d smooth decay reaches %.4f", flat_auc, max(dk_df$oos_2025_auc_o55)),
    x = "Half-Life H (Days)", y = "Locked 2025 OOS Over 5.5 K ROC AUC"
  ) +
  mlbr::theme_cyber()

out_png <- file.path(lake, "models/lab19_exp_decay_auc_diagnostic.png")
ggsave(out_png, p_lab19, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
cat(sprintf("Saved Dark Cyber Lab 19 diagnostic PNG to: %s\n", out_png))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 3:
# Why does H=7d perform worse than flat 30d while H=30d (90-day lookback) beats it cleanly?
cat("CHECKPOINT 3 PASS: Lab 19 completed cleanly!\n")

title: Lab 01 Work-Along: Aerodynamics, Trajectory Math & The Physics of Pitch Movement
section: 1. The Physical Coordinate System of Modern Baseball
text:
1. The Physical Coordinate System of Modern Baseball
To understand how modern pitch models (like Stuff+ and Pitching+) work, you have to understand the 3D Cartesian coordinate system that Statcast and Hawkeye use to track every baseball.
                  +z (Vertical Height above ground)
                   |
                   |      Strike zone: ~1.5 ft to 3.5 ft
                   |
                   +------- +y (Mound is at y = 60.5 ft; Release is at y = 50 ft)
                  /
                 /
                /
             +x (Horizontal: Catcher's perspective)
                Negative = Batter's inside (for Righty)
                Positive = Batter's outside (for Righty)
                Center of plate = 0.0 ft

The Key Dimensions to Memorize:

\(y = 60.5\text{ ft}\): The pitching rubber.
\(y = 50.0\text{ ft}\): The standard Statcast tracking origin (\(v_{x0}, v_{y0}, v_{z0}\) are measured here). By 50 ft, the pitcher has released the ball and it is in pure aerodynamic flight.
\(y = 1.417\text{ ft}\): The front edge of home plate. Home plate is a 17-inch pentagon (\(17\text{ inches} / 12 = 1.4167\text{ ft}\)). This is where the pitch crosses the plate and where the bat makes contact.
\(y = 0.0\text{ ft}\): The back point of home plate (the origin).



Why Velocities and Accelerations Have Surprising Signs:

\(v_y\) is ALWAYS negative: Because the ball travels from the pitcher (\(y = 50\)) toward home plate (\(y = 0\)), its position in \(y\) is decreasing over time. A 95 mph fastball has a release velocity \(v_{y0} \approx -139\text{ ft/s}\).
\(a_y\) is positive: Air drag resists the baseball’s forward motion. Since the ball is moving in the negative \(y\) direction, drag pushes in the positive \(y\) direction (\(a_y \approx +25\) to \(+35\text{ ft/s}^2\)). This drag slows the ball down between the hand and the plate.

title: Lab 01 Work-Along: Aerodynamics, Trajectory Math & The Physics of Pitch Movement
text:
2. Hand-Calculating Trajectory Physics in R
In workbooks/lab01_aerodynamics_workbook.R, we begin with Part 1: hand-calculating real parameters from a 98.5 mph Four-Seam fastball.

Step 2.1: Terminal Forward Velocity at Home Plate
Using the classic kinematic equation \(v_f^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a \Delta y\):
\[\Delta y = 1.417 - 50.0 = -48.583\text{ ft}\] \[v_{y,f} = -\sqrt{v_{y0}^2 + 2 \cdot a_y \cdot (-48.583)}\]
vy0 <- -144.2   # ft/s (98.3 mph at 50 ft)
ay  <- 31.4     # ft/s^2 (forward air drag)
delta_y <- 1.417 - 50.0
vy_f <- -sqrt(vy0^2 + 2 * ay * delta_y) # -133.2 ft/s (90.8 mph at plate)
The pitch loses 7.5 mph of forward speed purely due to atmospheric air drag.


Step 2.2: Time of Flight
\[t_{\text{flight}} = \frac{v_{y,f} - v_{y0}}{a_y}\]
t_flight <- (vy_f - vy0) / ay # 0.3503 seconds (350 ms)
The batter has just 350 milliseconds from release to contact to recognize pitch type, predict trajectory, and execute the swing.


Step 2.3: Terminal Vertical & Horizontal Velocity
\[v_{z,f} = v_{z0} + a_z \cdot t_{\text{flight}}\] \[v_{x,f} = v_{x0} + a_x \cdot t_{\text{flight}}\]


Step 2.4: Approach Angles (VAA and HAA)
\[\text{VAA} = \arctan\left(\frac{v_{z,f}}{-v_{y,f}}\right) \times \left(\frac{180}{\pi}\right)\] \[\text{HAA} = \arctan\left(\frac{v_{x,f}}{-v_{y,f}}\right) \times \left(\frac{180}{\pi}\right)\]

Preview of Tunneling Commitment Geometry (Covered in Full in Lab 03)
Now that we have mastered single-pitch trajectory aerodynamics, we advance to multi-pitch sequencing:

The Batter Commitment Point (\(y = 23.8\text{ ft}\)): Approximately 175 ms before plate contact, the human batter must commit their swing decision.
Tunneling Differential Distance (\(d_{\text{tunnel}}\)): \[d_{\text{commit}} = \sqrt{(x_{\text{pitch}} - x_{\text{fastball}})^2 + (z_{\text{pitch}} - z_{\text{fastball}})^2} \quad \text{at } y = 23.8\text{ ft}\] When a slider or sweeper breaks late after mirroring the fastball tunnel within \(2.5\text{ inches}\) at the commit point, chase swing rates increase by +9.3 percentage points.

title: Lab 10 Work-Along: Level 5 Market Edge, CLV & Fractional Kelly Sizing
section: 1. First-Principles Binary Contract Math: EV, Fractional Kelly & CLV
text:
1. First-Principles Binary Contract Math: EV, Fractional Kelly & CLV
For a binary market contract priced at implied probability \(q = 1 / O\) (e.g., 55¢ on Kalshi/Polymarket \(\Rightarrow O = 1.8182\)) against a calibrated Level 4 fair probability \(p\):
\[\text{EV} = p \cdot (O - 1) - (1 - p) = p \cdot O - 1\]
\[f^* = \min\!\left(f_{\max},\; c \cdot \max\!\left(0,\; \frac{p \cdot b - (1 - p)}{b}\right)\right), \quad b = O - 1\]
\[\text{CLV} = \frac{O_{\text{entry}}}{O_{\text{close}}} - 1\]
For example, buying a 55¢ contract with fair value 60% that closes at 58¢ yields EV = +9.09%, CLV = +5.45%, Full Kelly 11.11%, Quarter Kelly (c = 0.25) 2.78%, and Eighth Kelly (c = 0.125) 1.39%.

Lab 10 Diagnostic: Kelly Expected Log-Growth Curve g(f) & Over-Betting Cliff


Notice the asymmetric concavity of logarithmic utility: Quarter-Kelly (\(c = 0.25\)) and Eighth-Kelly (\(c = 0.125\)) sit on the steep left shoulder of \(g(f)\), capturing substantial compounding growth while slashing variance by \(16\times\) to \(64\times\). Conversely, over-estimating edge and betting past \(2 f^*\) pushes expected log-growth strictly negative even on positive-EV bets!

1. First-Principles Poisson Strikeout Prop Pricing
For a starting pitcher with pre-game expected strikeouts \(\lambda_i = \mathbb{E}[\text{SO}_i]\), exact binary Over/Under prop fair probabilities are: \[P(\text{SO}_i > 5.5) = 1 - \sum_{k=0}^{5} \frac{e^{-\lambda_i}\lambda_i^k}{k!}\] For an ace priced at \(\lambda = 6.0\) K, fair probabilities are 71.5% Over 4.5 K, 55.4% Over 5.5 K, and 39.4% Over 6.5 K.

section: 1. First-Principles Ballpark Factor Math & Shrinkage Mechanics
text:
1. First-Principles Ballpark Factor Math & Shrinkage Mechanics

Step 1.1: Raw Scoring Ratio & League Symmetry Adjustment
Single-season park factors measure the scoring rate in home games (both teams) versus road games (both teams):
\[\text{Ratio} = \frac{R_{\text{home}} / G_{\text{home}}}{R_{\text{road}} / G_{\text{road}}}\]
Because road games are played across the other 29 parks in the league, the exact 30-team league symmetry correction is:
\[\text{PF}_{\text{raw}} = \frac{30 \cdot \text{Ratio}}{29 + \text{Ratio}} \times 100\]


Step 1.2: 3-Year Weighted Regression & Empirical Bayes Shrinkage
\[\text{PF}_{\text{reg}} = 100 + (\text{PF}_{\text{3yr}} - 100) \times \frac{G_{\text{tot}}}{G_{\text{tot}} + M}\]
Where \(M = 40\) games for runs, \(M = 1500\) PA for home runs, and \(M = 2000\) PA for strikeouts, walks, and BABIP.

1. First-Principles Era-Neutralized PECOTA Similarity Math
To compare players across different offensive eras (e.g., 1963 Mickey Mantle vs. 2025 Aaron Judge), we standardize each stat into a seasonal \(z\)-score and compute the weighted Euclidean distance: \[d_{ij} = \sqrt{\sum_f \alpha_f \big(z_i^{(f)} - z_j^{(f)}\big)^2}, \qquad \text{Similarity} = 100 \cdot e^{-0.22 \cdot d_{ij}}\]

title: Data Proofs & Invariants
text:
Data lakes often degrade silently over time due to partial network failures, API rate limits, schema drift, or silent truncation. In baseball sabermetrics, a missing game or dropped column can invalidate WAR calculations, run expectancy matrices, and machine learning models.
mlbr provides a built-in verification suite (proof_lake()) that asserts 28 historical benchmarks, schema invariants, and physics boundaries across all 34+ million records.

title: Data Proofs & Invariants
text:
The 28 Automated Invariant Tests
The suite executes 5 test categories:

Benchmark Proving (Historical Ground Truth):

Aaron Judge 2022: Exactly 62 regular season Home Runs.
Barry Bonds 2001: Exactly 73 Home Runs.
Shohei Ohtani 2024: Exactly 54 Home Runs and 59 Stolen Bases (50/50 milestone).
Miguel Cabrera 2012: Triple Crown verification (.330 AVG, 44 HR, 139 RBI).
Pedro Martinez 2000: Historic pitching peak (1.74 ERA, 284 Strikeouts, 0.737 WHIP).

Crosswalk Integrity:

Chadwick Bureau cross-mapping between MLBAM, Retrosheet, and Baseball-Reference achieves >99.5% match rate on modern players.

Statcast Physical & Coordinate Invariants:

Pitch release velocity strictly between 35 mph (slow eephus) and 107 mph (Aroldis Chapman record).
Release coordinates (release_pos_x, release_pos_z) within real-world physical pitcher release windows.
Zero requests hitting the silent 25,000 row truncation cap.

Retrosheet Game & Play Invariants:

Innings recorded have \(\le 3\) outs.
Base runner occupancy state values strictly within \(0 \le \text{state} \le 7\).
Score values strictly non-negative.

Schema Completeness:

0 columns dropped across all tables.

section: Universal ID Join Recipes for AI Agents
text:
Universal ID Join Recipes for AI Agents
AI agents should utilize these verified SQL templates to combine high-speed Statcast telemetry with historical player profiles and team schedules:

1. Statcast Telemetry \(\leftrightarrow\) Universal Player Names & IDs
SELECT 
  sc.game_date,
  sc.pitch_type,
  sc.release_speed,
  sc.plate_x,
  sc.plate_z,
  cw.name_first || ' ' || cw.name_last AS pitcher_name,
  cw.key_retro,
  cw.key_bbref,
  cw.key_fangraphs
FROM v_statcast sc
LEFT JOIN v_chadwick_register cw 
  ON sc.pitcher = cw.key_mlbam
WHERE sc.game_date >= '2024-01-01'
LIMIT 10;


2. Fast Whiff Rate by Pitch Type
SELECT 
  pitch_type,
  count(*) as total_pitches,
  round(avg(release_speed), 1) as avg_mph,
  round(avg(case when description in ('swinging_strike', 'swinging_strike_blocked', 'missed_bunt') then 1.0 else 0.0 end) * 100, 2) as whiff_pct
FROM v_statcast
WHERE pitch_type IS NOT NULL AND release_speed IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY pitch_type
HAVING count(*) > 50000
ORDER BY total_pitches DESC;


3. Bidirectional Game Crosswalk (Retrosheet \(\leftrightarrow\) Statcast)
library(mlbr)
# Retrosheet GAME_ID -> Statcast game_pk
crosswalk_game("BOS202304150", to = "game_pk")
# Returns: 718576

# Statcast game_pk -> Retrosheet GAME_ID
crosswalk_game(718576, to = "GAME_ID")
# Returns: "BOS202304150"

title: Architecture & Storage
text:
Traditional sports analytics repositories suffer from two major anti-patterns: 1. Premature Aggregation / Column Dropping: Dropping columns during ingestion to save disk space, requiring full re-downloads when new research questions arise. 2. Monolithic Databases or Row-Oriented SQL Dumps: Storing 41.5M+ rows in .sql text dumps or single-writer database files (.duckdb, SQLite) creates file-lock contention, slow column scans, and tool lock-in.
mlbr resolves both by separating storage (ZSTD-compressed, key-sorted Apache Parquet) from query/compute (DuckDB SQL, R arrow, and Python pyarrow/polars).

title: Architecture & Storage
section: ADR-001: Storage Format, Compression & SQL vs. Parquet
text:
ADR-001: Storage Format, Compression & SQL vs. Parquet

What Is sql/01_statcast_features.sql?
sql/01_statcast_features.sql is a DuckDB SQL view definition (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_statcast_features ...), not a storage file. It stores zero data. Instead: - R/materialize_features.R executes the canonical view definition inside DuckDB and materializes the full 14.64M-row Silver table to ZSTD-compressed, key-sorted Parquet (data/features/statcast_features/). - mlbr::lake_register_features() mounts that Parquet dataset as v_statcast_features for sub-50ms SQL queries (falling back to live SQL evaluation over Bronze only when Silver isn’t materialized yet or force_dynamic = TRUE).

How Polars, Arrow & DuckDB Fit Together

In Memory (Zero-Copy Interchange): Polars uses Apache Arrow columnar buffers in memory (polars-arrow), the same memory layout used by DuckDB and R arrow via the Arrow C Data Interface. Moving query results between DuckDB SQL, R, and Python/Polars requires zero serialization copies.
On Disk (Canonical Storage): Polars and DuckDB both treat Apache Parquet as their primary analytical disk format. Combining COMPRESSION ZSTD with ROW_GROUP_SIZE = 100000 and ORDER BY (game_year, pitcher, game_date, game_pk, at_bat_number, pitch_number) shrinks the 14.64M-row Silver table from 1.6 GB (Snappy) down to 1.4 GB (ZSTD) while enabling Parquet min-max zone-map pruning (3.4× faster filtered reads).
Future Lakehouse Scaling (Delta Lake / Apache Iceberg): Because our canonical storage is already open Parquet, adding an Iceberg or Delta transaction log later requires zero data re-encoding if concurrent streaming writes grow.

title: Installation & Setup
text:
Dynamic Path Configuration
mlbr functions never require hardcoded paths. All routines resolve the active lake directory using default_lake(), which evaluates in order:

Explicit lake argument passed to functions (e.g., lake_status(lake = "..."))
Environment variable MLBR_DATA_PATH (set in ~/.Renviron)
R Option options(mlbr.path = "...")
Standard root /mnt/storage/Rprojects/mlbr if it exists
Current working directory getwd()

To configure your personal environment permanently, add the following to ~/.Renviron:
echo "MLBR_DATA_PATH=/mnt/storage/Rprojects/mlbr" >> ~/.Renviron

library(mlbr)

DuckDB Optimization & Threading
DuckDB is embedded and executes out-of-core operations without requiring a separate database server. For optimal performance on high-core machines like cbwdellr720:
con <- lake_duckdb()

# Configure DuckDB thread allocation and memory limit
DBI::dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA threads=16;")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA memory_limit='32GB';")

Chadwick Bureau Register: Universal cross-identifier mapping covering >527,000 players across MLB, MiLB, Retrosheet, Baseball-Reference, and Fangraphs.
NCAA & Minor League (MiLB) Data: Extended feeder systems and collegiate play tracking.

title: mlbr: Production Sabermetrics Data Lake
text:
Platform Architecture
mlbr utilizes a decoupled Lake-Warehouse architecture:
[ Data Providers ]
  ├── MLB Savant (Statcast per-pitch API)
  ├── Retrosheet / Chadwick Bureau (Git mirror & C tools)
  ├── FanGraphs (Leaderboards & Sabermetric Constants)
  └── Lahman / NCAA / MLB Meta
          │
          ▼
[ Ingestion & Adaptive Tier Ladder ] (R/ingest/*.R)
  - Month -> Week -> Day fallback (eliminates 25,000 row caps)
  - Exponential backoff & polite rate limiting
          │
          ▼
[ Storage Layer ] (data/raw/*.parquet)
  - Columnar Apache Parquet partitions
  - ZSTD / Snappy compression, dictionary encoding, sorted row groups
          │
          ▼
[ Zero-Copy Analytical Engine ] (DuckDB + mlbr R package)
  - Out-of-core streaming execution
  - Vectorized SIMD query processing
  - Direct integration with dplyr, tidymodels, and ggplot2
