title: Lab 18: Same-Game Parlay (SGP) Correlation Matrix & Copula Pricing
text:
Full Runnable Script (workbooks/lab18_sgp_correlation_copula_pricing_workbook.R)

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# ==============================================================================
# Lab 18: Same-Game Parlay (SGP) Correlation Matrix & Gaussian/Clayton Copulas
# Companion Work-Along Workbook for Study 18 (EXP-018)
# ==============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(mlbr)
  library(DBI)
  library(arrow)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

cat("=== Lab 18: SGP Correlation Matrix & Copula Pricing Engine ===\n")
lake <- mlbr::default_lake()
con  <- mlbr::lake_duckdb(lake)
on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), add = TRUE)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET memory_limit = '12GB';")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 1: First-Principles Sklar's Theorem & Clayton Copula
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Given marginal probabilities u, v in (0, 1) and dependence parameter theta > 0:
clayton_pos <- function(u, v, theta) {
  p <- (u^(-theta) + v^(-theta) - 1)^(-1 / theta)
  pmin(pmax(p, pmax(0, u + v - 1)), pmin(u, v))
}

# Example: Slugger HR (p = 0.14) + Team ML (p = 0.58)
u_hr <- 0.14; v_ml <- 0.58
p_ind_ex  <- u_hr * v_ml
p_clay_ex <- clayton_pos(u_hr, v_ml, theta = 0.45)
cat(sprintf("\nExample (HR 14%% + Team ML 58%%):\n  Naive Indep: %.2f%% (Fair Odds +%.0f)\n  Clayton (theta=0.45): %.2f%% (Fair Odds +%.0f, %.2fx lift)\n",
            100 * p_ind_ex, 100 * (1 / p_ind_ex - 1),
            100 * p_clay_ex, 100 * (1 / p_clay_ex - 1), p_clay_ex / p_ind_ex))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 1:
# Verify that clayton_pos(u, v, theta) ALWAYS obeys the Frechet-Hoeffding bounds:
# max(0, u + v - 1) <= C(u, v) <= min(u, v). What happens as theta -> 0 and theta -> Inf?
stopifnot(p_clay_ex >= max(0, u_hr + v_ml - 1) && p_clay_ex <= min(u_hr, v_ml))
cat("CHECKPOINT 1 PASS: Frechet-Hoeffding bounds verified.\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 2: Zero-Copy DuckDB SQL Query on Locked 2025 SGP Backtest
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
p_bt <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/sgp_copula_backtest_2024_2025.parquet")
p_ab <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/sgp_copula_ablation_metrics_2025.parquet")

sgp_sql <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf("
  SELECT
    sgp_label,
    COUNT(*) AS n_oos_2025,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(y_parlay), 2) AS actual_hit_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_ind), 2)    AS naive_ind_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(p_gauss), 2)  AS gauss_copula_pct,
    ROUND(AVG(p_gauss) / NULLIF(AVG(p_ind), 0), 3) AS fair_price_mult
  FROM read_parquet('%s')
  WHERE season = 2025
  GROUP BY sgp_label
  ORDER BY fair_price_mult DESC
", p_bt))

cat("\n=== Locked 2025 OOS SGP Pricing Summary (DuckDB Zero-Copy SQL) ===\n")
print(sgp_sql)

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 2:
# Inspect fair_price_mult > 1.0 (positive script) vs < 1.0 (negative script).
# Why does 'Home SP O5.5 K + Game Over 8.5' have fair_price_mult < 1.0 while
# 'Batter HR 1+ + Team ML' has fair_price_mult ~ 1.29x?
stopifnot(nrow(sgp_sql) == 7L)
cat("CHECKPOINT 2 PASS: All 7 two-leg SGP scripts queried via DuckDB SQL.\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 3: Dark Cyber Diagnostic Chart — Naive vs. Gaussian Copula Calibration
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ab_df <- arrow::read_parquet(p_ab) |>
  filter(model %in% c("M0_Naive_Independence", "M1_Gaussian_Copula"))

p_lab18 <- ggplot(ab_df, aes(x = reorder(sgp_label, abs(cal_bias_pp)), y = cal_bias_pp, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#f8fafc", linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("M0_Naive_Independence" = "#f43f5e", "M1_Gaussian_Copula" = "#38bdf8"),
    labels = c("M0: Naive Independence", "M1: Gaussian Copula"),
    name = "Pricing Model"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Lab 18 Diagnostic: Signed SGP Calibration Bias (Locked 2025 OOS)",
    subtitle = "Negative bias = model underprices true hit rate; Positive bias = model overprices",
    x = NULL, y = "Mean Predicted - Actual Hit Rate (Percentage Points)"
  ) +
  mlbr::theme_cyber()

out_png <- file.path(lake, "models/lab18_sgp_bias_diagnostic.png")
ggsave(out_png, p_lab18, width = 9.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
cat(sprintf("\nSaved Dark Cyber Lab 18 diagnostic PNG to: %s\n", out_png))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 3:
# Compare SGP1 (Home ML + F5 Home) vs SGP7 (Slot #2 + Slot #3 TB 2+).
# Why is residual teammate stack correlation only 1.03x once pre-game park, weather,
# and opposing starter HR% are already embedded in our EXP-017 marginals?
cat("CHECKPOINT 3 PASS: Lab 18 completed cleanly!\n")

title: Lab 05 Work-Along: Markov Decomposed Pitching+ & Swing Decisions
section: 1. First-Principles Markov Pitch Pricing & Zero-Mean Decision VoE
text:
1. First-Principles Markov Pitch Pricing & Zero-Mean Decision VoE
Instead of regressing directly on noisy base-out delta_run_exp, Study 05 predicts 5 clean transition probabilities (p_sw, p_cs, p_wh, p_fl, xwOBA|BIP) and prices them via exact 2015–2023 context-neutral 12-count linear weights (\(\beta_{\text{xwOBA}} = 0.8593\)):
\[\text{EV}_{\text{take}} = \hat{p}_{\text{cs}}\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}} + (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{cs}})\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{ball}}, \qquad \text{EV}_{\text{swing}} = \hat{p}_{\text{wh}}\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}} + (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{wh}})\,\text{EV}_{\text{contact}}\] \[\text{decision\_voe}_i = (I_{\text{swing},i} - \hat{p}_{\text{sw},i})\big(\text{EV}_{\text{swing},i} - \text{EV}_{\text{take},i}\big)\]
Because we subtract the league-average swing probability \(\hat{p}_{\text{sw},i}\), an average batter’s expected decision_voe equals 0.000 identically across every pitch type and count—eliminating pitch-mix bias!
In Part 1 of workbooks/lab05_decomposed_pitching_decisions_workbook.R: - 3-2 Full-Count Chase Slider (p_sw = 0.45, p_cs = 0.05, p_wh = 0.52, xwOBA = .220): Taking earns a strong positive reward (EV_take >> EV_swing), while chasing incurs a steep run penalty because 3-2 has a 0.6018 run Ball-Strike spread! - 1-0 Heart-Zone Fastball (p_sw = 0.78, p_cs = 0.96, p_wh = 0.14, xwOBA = .460): Attacking generates positive run value (EV_swing > EV_take), whereas passively watching a strike costs expected runs.

title: Lab 04 Work-Along: Marcel Projections, Delta-Method Aging & Physics Priors
section: 1. First-Principles Projection Math: Outs, Marcel & Uncertainty
text:
1. First-Principles Projection Math: Outs, Marcel & Uncertainty

Step 1.1: Never Treat Baseball Innings Pitched (.1/.2) as Decimals
FanGraphs and MLB box scores store 1 out as .1 and 2 outs as .2 (186.2 IP = 186.6667 decimal innings, NOT 186.20!). Always convert before sum-before-divide rate calculations:
\[\text{IP}_{\text{true}} = \lfloor \text{IP} \rfloor + \frac{\text{round}\big(10 \cdot (\text{IP} - \lfloor \text{IP} \rfloor)\big)}{3}\]


Step 1.2: Era-Adjusted Marcel Shrinkage & Tom Tango’s Age Factor
Recency weights \((w_1, w_2, w_3)\) (5/4/3 batters; 3/2/1 pitchers) pool multi-season excess skill above each season’s league average and regress toward the T-1 run environment using pre-backtest reliability denominator \(M_r\):
\[\hat{r}^{\text{Marcel}}_{i,T} = \mu_{\text{lg},T-1,g} + \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{3} w_k \, N_{i,T-k} \, (r_{i,T-k} - \mu_{\text{lg},T-k,g})}{\sum_{k=1}^{3} w_k \, N_{i,T-k} + M_r}\]
Running Part 1B demonstrates why sample-size shrinkage matters: - An established 27-year-old star (1,730 weighted PA across 3 years, .380/.365/.355 wOBA) earns 76.0% reliability weight → .355 regressed / .360 Tango-aged. - A hot 23-year-old rookie (180 PA, .380 wOBA) earns only 29.0% reliability weight → .332 regressed / .344 Tango-aged!


Step 1.3: Exposure-Calibrated 80% Uncertainty Bands
\[\text{CI}_{80\%}(i, T) = \hat{y}_{i,T} \pm 1.2816 \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{skill}}^2 + \frac{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{noise}}^2}{\widehat{N}_{i,T}}}\]
As projected playing time grows from 150 → 350 → 600 PA, the 80% wOBA half-width tightens from ±.048 → ±.039 → ±.036 (hitting 82.8% pitcher FIP and 81.4% batter wOBA empirical coverage on locked 2025 OOS!).

title: Lab 03 Work-Along: Commit-Point Pitch Tunneling & Stuff+ / Location+
section: 1. Exact y₀ = 50 ft → 23.8 ft Commit-Point Tunneling Math
text:
1. Exact y₀ = 50 ft → 23.8 ft Commit-Point Tunneling Math
A batter must commit their swing roughly 175 ms before plate arrival, corresponding to \(y_{\text{commit}} = 23.8\text{ ft}\) from home plate (front edge \(y_{\text{plate}} = 1.417\text{ ft}\)). Because Statcast velocity/acceleration vectors (vx0, vy0, vz0, ax, ay, az) are anchored at \(y_0 = 50.0\text{ ft}\), we propagate each pitch forward from 50.0 ft using exact constant-acceleration kinematics:
\[\Delta y = y_{\text{target}} - 50.0, \qquad v_y(y_{\text{target}}) = -\sqrt{v_{y0}^2 + 2 a_y \Delta y}, \qquad t = \frac{v_y(y_{\text{target}}) - v_{y0}}{a_y}\] \[x(t) = x_0 + v_{x0} t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_x t^2, \qquad z(t) = z_0 + v_{z0} t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_z t^2\]
From sequential same-PA pitch pairs \((p_{k-1}, p_k)\) we compute Commit-Point Tunnel Separation (\(d_{\text{tunnel}}\) at 23.8 ft), Home-Plate Separation (\(d_{\text{plate}}\) at 1.417 ft), and the Pavlidis/Judge Break-to-Tunnel Ratio (BTR):
\[d_{\text{tunnel}} = 12 \sqrt{(x_k - x_{k-1})^2 + (z_k - z_{k-1})^2}\Big|_{y=23.8}, \qquad \text{BTR} = \frac{d_{\text{plate}}}{\max(d_{\text{tunnel}},\, 0.5\text{ in})}\]
In Part 1 of lab03_tunneling_stuff_plus_workbook.R, a 96 mph Four-Seamer (361.0 ms flight) followed by an 86 mph Gyro Slider (402.6 ms flight) separates by only 1.50 inches at the commit point (23.8 ft) before diverging to 9.93 inches at home plate — a 6.63× late-break tunnel ratio!

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# ==============================================================================
# Lab 20: Dynamic In-Season Starter Workload (BF/GS) & Multivariate Copula-Kelly
# Companion Work-Along Workbook for Study 20 (EXP-020)
# ==============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(mlbr); library(DBI); library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
})

cat("=== Lab 20: Dynamic Workload K-Props & Multivariate Copula-Kelly ===\n")
lake <- mlbr::default_lake()
con  <- mlbr::lake_duckdb(lake)
on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), add = TRUE)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET memory_limit = '12GB';")

# PART 1: First-Principles 2-Asset Multivariate Kelly vs Independent Kelly
# Suppose two same-game bets each have EV mu = 0.05 and variance sigma^2 = 1.0, c = 0.25.
mu <- c(0.05, 0.05); c_frac <- 0.25
f_ind <- c_frac * mu / c(1.0, 1.0)
Sigma_pos <- matrix(c(1.0,  0.20,  0.20, 1.0), 2, 2)
Sigma_neg <- matrix(c(1.0, -0.20, -0.20, 1.0), 2, 2)
f_mv_pos <- as.numeric(c_frac * solve(Sigma_pos, mu))
f_mv_neg <- as.numeric(c_frac * solve(Sigma_neg, mu))
cat(sprintf("2-Bet Stake Sum — Indep: %.4f | Pos Corr (+0.20): %.4f (%+.1f%%) | Neg Corr (-0.20): %.4f (%+.1f%%)\n",
            sum(f_ind), sum(f_mv_pos), 100*(sum(f_mv_pos)/sum(f_ind)-1),
            sum(f_mv_neg), 100*(sum(f_mv_neg)/sum(f_ind)-1)))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 1:
# Verify that positive correlation strictly shrinks combined Kelly stake (f_mv_pos < f_ind)
# while negative correlation strictly expands it (f_mv_neg > f_ind).
stopifnot(sum(f_mv_pos) < sum(f_ind) && sum(f_mv_neg) > sum(f_ind))
cat("CHECKPOINT 1 PASS: Analytical Multivariate Kelly directionality verified.\n")

# PART 2: Zero-Copy DuckDB SQL Query on EXP-020 Dynamic Workload Ablation
p_kp <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/dynamic_workload_kprop_ablation_2025.parquet")
kp_sql <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf("
  SELECT model, half_life_days, has_dyn_bf,
         ROUND(theta_2024, 2) AS theta_nb,
         ROUND(oos_2025_nll, 5) AS oos_nll,
         ROUND(oos_2025_rmse, 4) AS oos_rmse,
         ROUND(oos_2025_auc_o55, 4) AS oos_auc_o55
  FROM read_parquet('%s')
  ORDER BY oos_2025_nll ASC
", p_kp))
print(kp_sql)

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 2:
# Notice how NegBin dispersion theta jumps from ~53 to ~84 when has_dyn_bf = TRUE!
# Why does modeling causal BF/GS cut extra-Poisson strikeout overdispersion by ~40%?
stopifnot(kp_sql$has_dyn_bf[1] == TRUE && kp_sql$theta_nb[1] > 75)
cat("CHECKPOINT 2 PASS: Dynamic BF/GS workload strictly leads locked 2025 OOS NLL & AUC.\n")

# PART 3: Dark Cyber Diagnostic Chart — NegBin Theta Jump from Dynamic BF/GS
p_lab20 <- ggplot(kp_sql, aes(x = reorder(model, theta_nb), y = theta_nb, fill = has_dyn_bf)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#38bdf8", "TRUE" = "#10b981"),
                    labels = c("Static Prior BF/GS", "+ Causal In-Season BF/GS"), name = "Workload Model") +
  labs(
    title = "Lab 20 Diagnostic: Negative Binomial Dispersion Theta (Higher = Less Unexplained Variance)",
    subtitle = "Adding causal in-season starter BF/GS explains ~40% of remaining strikeout overdispersion",
    x = NULL, y = "2024 MLE NegBin Dispersion Parameter (theta)"
  ) +
  mlbr::theme_cyber()

out_png <- file.path(lake, "models/lab20_workload_theta_diagnostic.png")
ggsave(out_png, p_lab20, width = 9.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
cat(sprintf("Saved Dark Cyber Lab 20 diagnostic PNG to: %s\n", out_png))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 3:
# Why should real-world Kelly portfolios always be benchmarked against live closing odds
# (via mlbr-market-archive.timer) rather than relying solely on synthetic prior-baseline books?
cat("CHECKPOINT 3 PASS: Lab 20 completed cleanly!\n")

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# ==============================================================================
# Lab 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions & Shannon Entropy (Seq+)
# Companion Work-Along Workbook for Study 21 (EXP-021)
# ==============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(mlbr); library(DBI); library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
})

cat("=== Lab 21: Pitch Sequencing, Markov Transitions & Shannon Entropy ===\n")
lake <- mlbr::default_lake()
con  <- mlbr::lake_duckdb(lake)
on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), add = TRUE)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET memory_limit = '12GB';")

# PART 1: First-Principles Shannon Entropy H(P) = -sum p * log2(p)
shannon_bits <- function(p) { p <- p[p > 0]; -sum(p * log2(p)) }
h_predictable <- shannon_bits(c(0.85, 0.10, 0.05))           # 85% fastball in 3-1
h_balanced    <- shannon_bits(c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25))     # 4-pitch equal mix
cat(sprintf("Shannon Entropy — Predictable 3-1 mix: %.3f bits | Balanced 4-pitch mix: %.3f bits\n",
            h_predictable, h_balanced))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 1:
# Verify that a uniform 4-pitch arsenal has exact entropy log2(4) = 2.000 bits,
# while an 85/10/5 predictable count mix collapses below 0.80 bits.
stopifnot(abs(h_balanced - 2.0) < 1e-12 && h_predictable < 0.80)
cat("CHECKPOINT 1 PASS: Information-theoretic Shannon entropy bounds verified.\n")

# PART 2: Zero-Copy DuckDB SQL Query on EXP-021 Gold Markov & Seq+ Tables
p_mk  <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/pitch_markov_transitions_2015_2025.parquet")
p_seq <- file.path(lake, "data/processed/pitcher_sequencing_entropy_2020_2025.parquet")

mk_sql <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf("
  SELECT prev_group, curr_group, n_pairs,
         ROUND(100.0 * whiff_rate, 2) AS whiff_pct,
         ROUND(mean_delta_velo, 1) AS avg_dv_mph
  FROM read_parquet('%s')
  ORDER BY whiff_pct DESC
", p_mk))
print(mk_sql)

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 2:
# Inspect why Breaking -> Breaking leads raw whiff% (35.2%) and explain why we MUST
# control for count & single-pitch location (M2 - M1) to isolate true sequencing skill!
stopifnot(nrow(mk_sql) == 9L && sum(mk_sql$n_pairs) > 5000000L)
cat("CHECKPOINT 2 PASS: All 9 Markov transitions queried across 5.47M+ pairs.\n")

# PART 3: Dark Cyber Diagnostic Chart — Top 12 2025 MLB Pitchers by Seq+
top12 <- arrow::read_parquet(p_seq) |>
  filter(season == 2025L, n_paired_swings >= 300L, !is.na(player_name)) |>
  arrange(desc(seq_plus)) |>
  head(12)

p_lab21 <- ggplot(top12, aes(x = reorder(player_name, seq_plus), y = seq_plus, fill = count_entropy_bits)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(100, 155)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Count\nEntropy\n(bits)") +
  labs(
    title = "Lab 21 Diagnostic: Top 12 MLB Pitch Sequencers in 2025 (Seq+, min 300 paired swings)",
    subtitle = "Orthogonal whiff-value added by sequencing & eye-level shifts above full pitch physics + location",
    x = NULL, y = "Sequence+ (Seq+, 100 = 2024 MLB Avg)"
  ) +
  mlbr::theme_cyber()

out_png <- file.path(lake, "models/lab21_top12_seq_plus_diagnostic.png")
ggsave(out_png, p_lab21, width = 9.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
cat(sprintf("Saved Dark Cyber Lab 21 diagnostic PNG to: %s\n", out_png))

# MENTOR CHECKPOINT 3:
# Compare Tarik Skubal (1.965 bits entropy, 130.5 Seq+) vs Tommy Kahnle (0.593 bits, 151.8 Seq+).
# How can a reliever with low pitch-type entropy still post elite Seq+ via vertical eye-level & tunnel shifts?

title: Study 08: Level 3 Team Run Creation (David Smyth BaseRuns), Dynamic Pythagenpat & 2026 Standings Simulator
text:
2. Domain Problem & Non-Linear Run Theory
Linear weights (wOBA, wRAA) treat every offensive event as additive. In reality, baseball scoring is multiplicative: getting on base (\(A\)) only converts into runs proportionally to the lineup’s ability to advance runners (\(B\)) before the defense records outs (\(C\)), plus self-scoring home runs (\(D\)). David Smyth’s BaseRuns models this exact physical structure, while Smyth & Patriot’s Pythagenpat adapts the win-expectation exponent \(\gamma\) continuously to each era’s run-scoring environment.

title: Study 08: Level 3 Team Run Creation (David Smyth BaseRuns), Dynamic Pythagenpat & 2026 Standings Simulator
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline
\[\text{BaseRuns} = \frac{A \cdot B}{B + C} + D, \qquad \gamma = \left(\frac{RS + RA}{G}\right)^{0.287}, \qquad W\% = \frac{RS^\gamma}{RS^\gamma + RA^\gamma}\]
Game-by-game 2026 schedule probabilities combine each club’s perturbed season true-talent win percentage via Tom Tango’s Log5 odds ratio layered with neutral home-field advantage (\(\text{HFA} = 0.535\)).

title: The 24 Base-Out Run Expectancy Matrix (RE24)
text:
At any given moment in a baseball game, the state of the half-inning can be partitioned into 24 discrete base-out states: - 3 Out States: 0 outs, 1 out, 2 outs - 8 Base Occupancy States: Empty (___), 1st (1__), 2nd (_2_), 1st & 2nd (12_), 3rd (__3), 1st & 3rd (1_3), 2nd & 3rd (_23), and Bases Loaded (123).
Run Expectancy (RE) is the expected number of runs that will be scored from that point until the end of the half-inning. It forms the foundational bedrock of modern sabermetrics: \[\Delta \text{RE} = \text{RE}_{\text{state}_{t+1}} - \text{RE}_{\text{state}_t} + \text{Runs Scored on Play}\]
This difference (\(\Delta \text{RE}\)) is the empirical Run Value of any baseball event (single, strikeout, stolen base, double play), from which Linear Weights, wOBA constants, and WAR are derived.

title: The 24 Base-Out Run Expectancy Matrix (RE24)
text:
At any given moment in a baseball game, the state of the half-inning can be partitioned into 24 discrete base-out states: - 3 Out States: 0 outs, 1 out, 2 outs - 8 Base Occupancy States: Empty (___), 1st (1__), 2nd (_2_), 1st & 2nd (12_), 3rd (__3), 1st & 3rd (1_3), 2nd & 3rd (_23), and Bases Loaded (123).
Run Expectancy (RE) is the expected number of runs that will be scored from that point until the end of the half-inning. It forms the foundational bedrock of modern sabermetrics: \[\Delta \text{RE} = \text{RE}_{\text{state}_{t+1}} - \text{RE}_{\text{state}_t} + \text{Runs Scored on Play}\]

title: The 24 Base-Out Run Expectancy Matrix (RE24)
text:
Extracting Plays via DuckDB
Using mlbr’s zero-copy DuckDB connection, we compute future half-inning runs directly over a sample of 150,000 modern regular season plays:


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  .libPaths(c("/mnt/storage/R/library", .libPaths()))
  library(mlbr)
  library(duckdb)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tidyr)
  library(knitr)
  library(viridis)
})

con <- lake_duckdb()

# Compute base-out state and future inning runs using window functions
re24_raw <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH play_events AS (
    SELECT 
      GAME_ID,
      TRY_CAST(INN_CT AS INTEGER) AS inn,
      BAT_HOME_ID,
      TRY_CAST(EVENT_ID AS INTEGER) AS event_id,
      TRY_CAST(OUTS_CT AS INTEGER) AS outs,
      CASE WHEN BASE1_RUN_ID != '' AND BASE1_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
      CASE WHEN BASE2_RUN_ID != '' AND BASE2_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 2 ELSE 0 END +
      CASE WHEN BASE3_RUN_ID != '' AND BASE3_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 4 ELSE 0 END AS base_state,
      COALESCE(TRY_CAST(EVENT_RUNS_CT AS INTEGER), 0) AS runs_scored
    FROM retro_plays
    WHERE TRY_CAST(OUTS_CT AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 0 AND 2
      AND TRY_CAST(INN_CT AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1 AND 9
    USING SAMPLE 150000 (reservoir)
  ),
  half_innings AS (
    SELECT 
      *,
      SUM(runs_scored) OVER (PARTITION BY GAME_ID, inn, BAT_HOME_ID) AS total_inn_runs,
      SUM(runs_scored) OVER (
        PARTITION BY GAME_ID, inn, BAT_HOME_ID 
        ORDER BY event_id 
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS runs_before
    FROM play_events
  )
  SELECT 
    outs,
    base_state,
    COALESCE(total_inn_runs - COALESCE(runs_before, 0), 0) AS rem_runs
  FROM half_innings
  WHERE outs BETWEEN 0 AND 2
    AND base_state BETWEEN 0 AND 7;
")

cat(sprintf("Extracted %d valid base-out state transitions.\n", nrow(re24_raw)))


Extracted 146719 valid base-out state transitions.

title: The 24 Base-Out Run Expectancy Matrix (RE24)
text:
The Empirical RE24 Matrix
We group by base_state and outs to calculate mean run expectancy:


Code
state_labels <- c(
  "0" = "___ (Bases Empty)",
  "1" = "1__ (Runner on 1st)",
  "2" = "_2_ (Runner on 2nd)",
  "3" = "12_ (1st & 2nd)",
  "4" = "__3 (Runner on 3rd)",
  "5" = "1_3 (1st & 3rd)",
  "6" = "_23 (2nd & 3rd)",
  "7" = "123 (Bases Loaded)"
)

re24_summary <- re24_raw %>%
  group_by(base_state, outs) %>%
  summarize(
    exp_runs = mean(rem_runs),
    sample_n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(base_desc = state_labels[as.character(base_state)])

re24_matrix <- re24_summary %>%
  select(base_desc, outs, exp_runs) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = outs, values_from = exp_runs, names_prefix = "outs_")

knitr::kable(
  re24_matrix,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Base State", "0 Outs", "1 Out", "2 Outs"),

NoteKey Insights from RE24




The Cost of an Out: Going from 0 outs to 1 out with bases empty drops run expectancy by 0.23 runs; going from 1 out to 2 outs drops it by another 0.16 runs.
Bases Loaded Premium: With 0 outs, a bases-loaded situation yields ~2.29 expected runs—over 4.5x more than bases empty (0.50 runs).
The True Value of a Home Run: A solo home run is worth exactly \(1.000 + (0.500 - 0.500) = 1.000\) runs. But on average across all base states, a home run produces +1.40 runs in net value.

title: Study 13: Pitcher Stamina, In-Game Fastball Velocity Decay & Dynamic Rolling Bullpen Fatigue Engine
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
In Study 13, mlbr quantifies two critical dynamic fatigue effects used by pro MLB front offices and sharp game-pricing syndicates across 2018–2025:








Pillar
Validated Result (2018–2025)
Sabermetric & Market Implication




Starter Velocity Decay (1.44M Fastballs)
Starters drop -0.11 mph (21–40), -0.21 mph (41–60), and -0.43 mph (61–80); past pitch 100, survivorship masks velocity (-0.04 mph) while Pitcher RV/100 degrades to +0.35 (worst of all 6 bins).
Confirms why TTO familiarity + late-inning fatigue drives sharp live-betting and F5-vs-Full-Game divergences.


Zero-Leakage Rolling Bullpen Fatigue (35,812 Team-Games)
Pre-test (2018–2023, n = 26,094) slope: +0.0516 R/G per +100 trailing 3-day reliever pitches; Taxed (181+) bullpens allow 2.025 R/G in innings 6–9 vs. 1.892 R/G for Light (61–100).
Directly quantifies the pre-game penalty of a gassed bullpen for Level 4/5 game and totals pricing.


Starter Velocity Retention Leaderboard (2025)
Rare “ramping” workhorses (Carlos Rodón +1.18 mph, Luis Severino +0.89 mph, Sandy Alcántara +0.51 mph, -0.46 late RV/100) hold velocity past pitch 75.
Identifies starters who outperform generic TTO-3 fatigue curves in innings 5–7.

title: Study 13: Pitcher Stamina, In-Game Fastball Velocity Decay & Dynamic Rolling Bullpen Fatigue Engine
text:
2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Fatigue Mechanics
Pre-game models that treat every club’s bullpen as a static season-long FIP ignore acute 3-day workload spikes (extra-inning games, short starts, doubleheaders) that force managers to deploy lower-leverage middle relievers. Similarly, starter velocity pacing exhibits a classic non-linear interplay between physiological fatigue (peaking at pitches 61–80) and survivorship/adrenaline (“emptying the tank” on the final batter past pitch 80).

EXP-001-AERODYNAMICS: Trajectory Aerodynamics, Approach Angles (VAA/HAA) & Whiff Lift
Tier: Level 1: Pitch Physics & Quality | Status: VALIDATED | Updated: 2026-11-16

Derived full-population terminal flight velocities at y=1.417 ft, VAA, HAA, plate_x_norm, and attack zones over 14.64M pitches in DuckDB. Proved flat VAA (VAA_diff > +1.5 deg) produces +52% relative lift in Four-Seam fastball whiff rate.

All tree models beat empirical and analytical Ridge baselines on locked 2025-2026 run value and swing-and-miss whiff deception; mlbr Stuff+ hits split-half r = 0.975 in 100 regular-season pitches (vs. 0.078 for Raw RV/100), achieves YoY r = 0.878 (vs. ERA r = 0.188), and correlates at r = 0.817 with FanGraphs Pitching+.


Verified Formulas
commit_time_t_dec: (-sqrt(vy0^2 + 2*ay*(23.8 - 50.0)) - vy0) / ay
x50_reconstruction: plate_x - vx0*t_plate - 0.5*ax*t_plate^2
tunnel_dist_in: 12 * sqrt((x_dec_N - x_dec_{N-1})^2 + (z_dec_N - z_dec_{N-1})^2)
break_to_tunnel_ratio_bp: post_tunnel_break_in / GREATEST(tunnel_dist_in, 1.0)
plate_to_tunnel_ratio: plate_sep_in / GREATEST(tunnel_dist_in, 1.0)

EXP-005-DECOMPOSED-PITCHING-DECISIONS: Context-Neutral Markov Decomposed Pitching+ & Pitch-Level Batter Process Engine (Decision+, BatControl+, Contact+)
Tier: Level 1: Pitch Physics & Quality | Status: VALIDATED | Updated: 2026-11-20

Replaced single-head raw delta_run_exp regression with a strictly chronological 5-head Markov probability decomposition (p_swing, p_cstr|take, p_whiff|swing, p_foul|contact, E[xwOBA|BIP]) priced via 2015-2023 context-neutral 12-count linear weights. Decomp Pitching+ beat Study 03 Pitching+ on locked 2024->2025 SIERA (-0.5040 vs -0.4984), Hawk-Eye 2020-2023 beat 2015-2023 on all 5 pitch-level validation heads, and pitch-level Batter Decision+ achieved r=0.8464 YoY stability and r=+0.5583 forecasting 2025 BB% (crushing Z-O% proxy +0.3994).


Verified Formulas
bip_rv_map: delta_run_exp ~ factor(count_id) + 0.8593 * xwoba (fit strictly on 2015-2023 BIPs)
ev_take: p_cs * rv_strike(b,s) + (1 - p_cs) * rv_ball(b,s)
ev_swing: p_wh * rv_strike(b,s) + (1 - p_wh) * (p_fl * rv_foul(b,s) + (1 - p_fl) * rv_bip(b,s,xwoba_hat))
decision_voe: (is_swing - p_sw_hat) * (ev_swing - ev_take)
bat_ctrl_rv: is_swing * (p_wh_hat - is_whiff) * (ev_contact - rv_strike(b,s))
contact_rv: is_bip * 0.8593 * (xwoba - xwoba_hat)
batter_process_rv: decision_voe + bat_ctrl_rv + contact_rv

EXP-004-PLAYER-PROJECTIONS: Chronological True-Talent Player Projections: Marcel, Delta-Method Aging & Tier 1 Physics Priors
Tier: Level 2: Player Projections | Status: VALIDATED | Updated: 2026-11-20

Built audit-hardened Tier 2 chronological true-talent projection engine for MLB pitchers and batters across 2002-2027 (10-year rolling Tango Marcel vs. Midpoint Delta-Method Aging 2016-2025, 7-year Statcast Physics 2019-2025, locked 2024->2025 FanGraphs OOS with Stage-2 Residual mlbr Stuff+ and Hawk-Eye Bat Tracking, and secondary 2025->2026 Regular-Season Statcast OOS). Introduced Pulled Air-Ball%, Zone-Chase Selectivity (Z-O Swing%, SEAGER-inspired proxy), Sweet-Spot%, Fastball Velocity Momentum, sum-before-shrink seasonal PVI, and exposure-calibrated 80% uncertainty bands.


Verified Formulas
exact_ip_true: FLOOR(IP) + ROUND((IP - FLOOR(IP)) * 10) / 3
baseball_age_july1: Season - birth_year - I(birth_month >= 7)
tango_marcel_age: age <= 29: 1 + 0.006*(29 - age); age > 29: 1 / (1 + 0.003*(age - 29)) + Step 6 rebaselining
marcel_rate_shrinkage: mu_lg_{T-1,g} + SUM(w_k * N_{T-k} * (r_{T-k} - mu_lg_{T-k,g})) / (SUM(w_k * N_{T-k}) + M_r)
delta_aging_midpoint: lm(delta ~ ns(age - 0.5, knots = c(24.5, 30.5)), weights = 2*N_{s-1}*N_s/(N_{s-1}+N_s)) + linear boundary extrapolation
pulled_air_pct: mean(LA >= 10 & ((stand=='R' & spray < -15 deg) | (stand=='L' & spray > +15 deg)))
zone_chase_selectivity: Z-Swing% - O-Swing% (SEAGER-inspired box-zone proxy)
uncertainty_se: sqrt(sigma_skill^2 + sigma_noise^2 / exposure)

In Study 11, mlbr unlocks 1,043,401 competitive Hawk-Eye swings (>= 60 mph, 2023–2026) and 4.5M+ pitcher release arm_angle observations (2020–2026) already stored in Bronze v_statcast. Across strictly chronological out-of-sample tests:

Arm Angle r = 0.963, Swing Length r = 0.928, Bat Speed r = 0.923, IVB Above Slot r = 0.885, Attack Angle r = 0.847 vs. ISO 0.591, wOBA 0.448, BABIP 0.299.
Biomechanical sensors capture true-talent mechanics with minimal luck noise, stabilizing far faster than outcome stats.


Locked 2025 OOS Batter Projection Lift (n = 305)
Trained strictly on 2023 -> 2024: adding bat_speed + blast_rate + swing_length cuts locked 2025 OOS ISO RMSE by 3.66% (0.0444 -> 0.0427) and wOBA RMSE by 1.57% (0.0317 -> 0.0312).
Directly upgrades Level 2 true-talent power projections and Level 4 daily lineup scoring.


Locked 2024–2025 OOS 4-Seam Whiff Ablation (n = 219,655 swings)
Adding arm_angle + ivb_above_slot (slot expectation fit strictly on 2020–2023) drops Log-Loss 0.52156 -> 0.51721 (-0.00435) and jumps ROC AUC +0.0302 (0.5615 -> 0.5917).
Release slot deception is a first-order determinant of fastball swing-and-miss above raw velocity and raw IVB.

title: Study 11: Hawk-Eye Bat-Tracking (1.04M Competitive Swings) & Pitcher Arm-Slot Biomechanics
text:
2. Domain Problem & Theoretical Biomechanics
Traditional box-score stats (wOBA, ISO, BABIP) confound hitter skill with batted-ball luck, ballpark dimensions, and defensive positioning. Similarly, raw pitch velocity and raw induced vertical break (IVB) ignore the perceptual reference frame of a pitcher’s release slot (arm_angle): a 17.5" IVB fastball from a 31° low three-quarters slot produces a dramatically flatter Vertical Approach Angle (VAA) and far more deception than an identical 17.5" fastball from a 60° over-the-top slot.

title: Study 11: Hawk-Eye Bat-Tracking (1.04M Competitive Swings) & Pitcher Arm-Slot Biomechanics
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline

3.1 Collision Physics, Squared-Up Rate & Blast Rate
\[\text{MaxEV} = 1.23 \cdot v_{\text{bat}} + 0.2116 \cdot v_{\text{release}}, \qquad \text{SqUp} = \frac{\text{EV}}{\text{MaxEV}}\] \[\text{Blast} = \mathbb{I}\!\big(\text{SqUp} \ge 0.80 \;\wedge\; v_{\text{bat}} + 100 \cdot \text{SqUp} \ge 164\big)\]


3.2 Slot-Adjusted Vertical Ride (ivb_above_slot)
\[\widehat{\text{IVB}}(\phi) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \phi + \beta_2 \phi^2 \;\; (\text{fit on } 2020\text{–}2023), \qquad \text{IVB}_{\text{above\_slot}} = 12 \cdot \text{pfx\_z} - \widehat{\text{IVB}}(\phi)\]


3.3 Reproducible Zero-Copy DuckDB SQL Query
SET memory_limit = '12GB';
SELECT
  game_year,
  COUNT(*) AS n_comp_swings,
  ROUND(AVG(TRY_CAST(bat_speed AS DOUBLE)), 2) AS mean_bs_mph,
  ROUND(AVG(TRY_CAST(swing_length AS DOUBLE)), 2) AS mean_sl_ft,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN TRY_CAST(bat_speed AS DOUBLE) >= 75.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END), 1) AS fast_swing_pct
FROM v_statcast
WHERE game_year BETWEEN 2023 AND 2026
  AND game_type = 'R'
  AND TRY_CAST(bat_speed AS DOUBLE) >= 60.0
GROUP BY game_year
ORDER BY game_year;

title: Non-Linear xwOBA & The Barrel Landscape
text:
In the Statcast era, a batter’s quality of contact is measured by two primary physical parameters: 1. Launch Speed (Exit Velocity, mph): How hard the ball leaves the bat. 2. Launch Angle (degrees): The vertical trajectory of the batted ball.
Traditional batting average and slugging percentage are heavily confounded by defense, ballpark dimensions, and random weather variation. Statcast’s Expected Weighted On-Base Average (xwOBA) and Expected Batting Average (xBA) remove these artifacts by modeling outcomes purely as a function of launch velocity and angle.
In this study, we train a 2D Generalized Additive Model (GAM) thin-plate spline to construct the continuous probability landscape of hits and visualize the famous Statcast “Barrel” zone.

title: Non-Linear xwOBA & The Barrel Landscape
text:
Data Extraction via DuckDB
We pull all fair batted ball events with valid exit velocity and launch angle metrics from the mlbr data lake:


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  .libPaths(c("/mnt/storage/R/library", .libPaths()))
  library(mlbr)
  library(duckdb)
  library(dplyr)
  library(mgcv)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(viridis)
  library(scales)
})

con <- lake_duckdb()

# Sample 35,000 batted balls
batted_df <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT 
    events,
    launch_speed,
    launch_angle,
    CASE 
      WHEN events IN ('single', 'double', 'triple', 'home_run') THEN 1 
      ELSE 0 
    END AS is_hit,
    CASE 
      WHEN events = 'single' THEN 0.89
      WHEN events = 'double' THEN 1.27
      WHEN events = 'triple' THEN 1.62
      WHEN events = 'home_run' THEN 2.10
      ELSE 0.0
    END AS woba_val
  FROM statcast
  WHERE type = 'X'
    AND launch_speed BETWEEN 45 AND 120
    AND launch_angle BETWEEN -50 AND 80
    AND events IS NOT NULL
  USING SAMPLE 35000 (reservoir);
")

cat(sprintf("Loaded %d batted balls with complete exit velocity and launch angle.\n", nrow(batted_df)))


Loaded 1508 batted balls with complete exit velocity and launch angle.

NoteKey Physical Takeaways




The Launch Angle Sweet Spot: Regardless of exit velocity, balls hit higher than 50° (popups) or lower than -10° (weak grounders) produce almost zero expected value.
Non-Linear Exit Velocity Returns: Below 90 mph, launch angle has modest effect on extra-base hits. Above 98 mph, each additional mph exponentially expands the allowable launch angle range for home runs.

title: Study 02: 4-Quadrant Platoon Physics & Situational Pitching Effectiveness
text:
1. Business & Scientific Understanding

1.1 Why Platoon Physics Drives Prediction Market Edge
Public sportsbooks and prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) routinely anchor pitcher valuation on lagging, season-aggregate metrics such as ERA, FIP, or overall K%. Those aggregates implicitly average over a pitcher’s historical mix of left- and right-handed opponents.
In reality, a pitcher’s effectiveness is not a single scalar—it is a 4-quadrant physical interaction between release geometry, aerodynamic break vector, and batter swing plane: - Same-Hand Quadrants (RvR, LvL): Glove-side breaking pitches (ST, SL) sweep away from the batter’s barrel and visual depth plane. - Opposite-Hand Quadrants (RvL, LvR): That same glove-side pitch breaks into the batter’s swing path, forcing pitchers to rely on arm-side deception (CH, FS), vertical ride (FF), or steep drop (CU).
When an opposing manager stacks 6–7 opposite-handed hitters against a slider/sweeper-dependent starter, the pitcher’s true-talent strikeout rate and contact suppression degrade immediately—creating mispriced Over/Under totals, strikeout props, and moneylines.


1.2 Hypotheses

Hypothesis 2.1 (Batter-Perspective Break Symmetry): Platoon effectiveness is governed physically by horizontal break relative to the batter (hb_away_in), not pitcher handedness alone.
Hypothesis 2.2 (Multi-Metric Evaluation Invariant): Evaluating pitches on Whiff% alone systematically undervalues Sinkers (SI), which suppress xwOBA and drive positive RV/100 via ground balls (GB%) in same-hand matchups.
Hypothesis 2.3 (Platoon Vulnerability Index, PVI): Pitchers lacking an opposite-hand offspeed weapon (CH/FS) exhibit large PVI_csw and PVI_xwoba gaps and amplified 3rd-time-through-the-order (TTO) damage.

title: Study 02: 4-Quadrant Platoon Physics & Situational Pitching Effectiveness
text:
3. Mathematical Derivation: Symmetric Platoon Coordinates
To compare left- and right-handed pitchers on a unified geometric basis, Silver (v_statcast_features) defines two complementary horizontal break coordinates from Statcast pfx_x (hb_in = pfx_x * 12):

Pitcher-Perspective Horizontal Break (hb_glove_in): \[\text{hb\_glove\_in} = \text{hb\_in} \times \begin{cases} -1 & \text{if } \text{p\_throws} = \text{L} \\ +1 & \text{if } \text{p\_throws} = \text{R} \end{cases}\] Positive values always indicate glove-side break (ST, SL, FC); negative values always indicate arm-side run (SI, CH, FS).
Batter-Perspective Horizontal Break (hb_away_in): \[\text{hb\_away\_in} = \text{hb\_in} \times \begin{cases} -1 & \text{if } \text{stand} = \text{L} \\ +1 & \text{if } \text{stand} = \text{R} \end{cases}\] Positive values always break away from the batter; negative values always break in toward the batter.
Platoon Vulnerability Index (PVI): \[\text{PVI}_{\text{xwOBA}} = \text{xwOBA}_{\text{opp}} - \text{xwOBA}_{\text{same}}, \qquad \text{PVI}_{\text{CSW}} = \text{CSW\%}_{\text{same}} - \text{CSW\%}_{\text{opp}}\]

2. Domain Problem & Player-Prop Market Structure
Why do sharp syndicates allocate substantial capital to Pitcher Strikeout Props? Because a starting pitcher’s strikeout total is directly governed by 6 compounding, pre-game observable physical & environmental factors: (1) the starter’s own K% & batters-faced stamina (BF/GS), (2) the exact 9 batters in today’s opposing lineup (opp_lineup_k), (3) starter arm-slot vertical ride (ivb_above_slot, EXP-011), (4) ballpark strikeout factor (pf_so, EXP-006), (5) home-plate umpire strike-zone K tendency (BASE4_UMP_ID), and (6) the starting catcher’s prior-season framing (csaa_per_1000, EXP-012).

title: Study 05: Context-Neutral Decomposed Pitching+ & Pitch-Level Batter Process Engine
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
Study 03 (EXP-003) regressed directly on single-pitch pitcher_run_exp (-delta_run_exp), reaching \(r = -0.4984\) (exposure-weighted) on locked 2024 → 2025 SIERA. Raw delta_run_exp entangles pitch quality with base-out state (a bases-loaded walk costs ~0.85 runs vs. ~0.29 bases empty) and single-pitch BABIP luck. In Study 05, we replace single-head run-value regression with a 5-head Markov probability decomposition (p_swing, p_cstr|take, p_whiff|swing, p_foul|contact, E[xwOBA|BIP]) priced via exact context-neutral 12-count linear weights across 8,105,884 Regular-Season pitches (2015–2026). Crucially, the exact same locked probability surface simultaneously yields a zero-mean Pitch-Level Batter Process Engine (Decision+, BatControl+, Contact+, BatterProcess+) that directly upgrades Study 04’s aggregate Zone-Chase (Z-O%) proxy.








Pillar
Validated Out-of-Sample Result
Sabermetric & Forecasting Implication




Markov Pitch Decomposition (2024 → 2025 Pitchers, \(N = 329\))
Decomp Pitching+ improves weighted SIERA forecasting to w_r = -0.5040 (beating Study 03 -0.4984 and FanGraphs Stuff+ -0.4753, closing two-thirds of the gap to FanGraphs Pitching+ -0.5165). Decomp Pitch+Tunnel (-0.4986) jumps +0.0132 over Study 03 Pitch+Tunnel (-0.4854).
Pricing probabilities through context-neutral 12-count weights eliminates base-out leverage noise; adding v_statcast_tunneling improves p_whiff, p_cstr, and p_foul validation logloss.


Pure Command Breakout (Decomp Location+ → 2025 BB%)
Decomp Location+ achieves w_r = -0.3273 forecasting next-year BB% — nearly 2× commercial FanGraphs Pitching+ (-0.1801) and 3.8× Study 03 Pitching+ (-0.0853).
Modeling p_cstr|take (0.1558 val logloss) and p_swing separately with 3-2 leverage (0.6018 run spread) isolates true walk-prevention command cleanly.


Hawk-Eye Sensor Homogeneity (2020–2023 vs. 2015–2023)
Decomp_Stuff_HawkEye (2.40M pitches) strictly beat Decomp_Stuff_Full (5.97M pitches) on all 5 pitch-level 2024 validation heads (sw, cs, wh, fl, xwOBA) and matched season-level SIERA (-0.4169 vs. -0.4187) on 60% fewer rows.
Confirms Hawk-Eye era tracking calibration homogeneity outweighs raw TrackMan volume at the pitch level.


True Pitch-Level Batter Decision+ (2024 → 2025, \(N = 265\))
Decision+ (Zero-Mean Value Over Expected Choice) achieves r_YoY = 0.8464 (#1 most stable batter process metric!) and predicts 2025 BB% at w_r = +0.5583 — crushing Study 04’s Z-O% proxy (+0.3994) by +0.159!
Context- and pitch-quality-weighted swing decisions eliminate pitch-mix bias and isolate plate discipline far more accurately than binary zone boxes.


Additive BatterProcess+ & BatControl+ (\(N = 265\))
BatControl+ hits r_YoY = 0.8179 (0.8246 on untouched 2025 → 2026) and forecasts 2025 K% at w_r = -0.7240. BatterProcess+ forecasts 2025 wOBA at w_r = +0.5256, strictly beating prior-year raw wOBA (0.4920) purely from pitch process.
Honest ablation disclosure: nested F-test over wOBA + xwOBA + Z-O% yields \(p = 0.7868\) on 1-year wOBA (xwOBA captures most BIP damage), while Decision+ and BatControl+ dominate component skill separation (BB%, K%, YoY stability).

title: Study 05: Context-Neutral Decomposed Pitching+ & Pitch-Level Batter Process Engine
text:
2. Domain Problem & Sabermetric Theory
Why did Study 03’s single-head delta_run_exp model leave signal on the table — and how does fixing it simultaneously unlock pitch-level batter evaluation?

Base-Out State Contamination in Raw delta_run_exp: A 3-2 ball with the bases loaded and 2 outs carries -0.85 pitcher runs, whereas the exact same pitch with bases empty carries -0.29 runs. Training an L2 loss tree ensemble on raw delta_run_exp gives high-leverage innings ~8× squared-error weight and mixes situational context into pitch-quality splits.
Non-Linearity of Pitch Outcomes: Different physical mechanisms govern different sub-events:

p(called strike | take) depends sharply on plate_x_norm, sz_norm_z, count, and late break (0.1486 logloss!).
p(whiff | swing) depends heavily on velocity, VAA/IVB, and commit-point tunneling (v_statcast_tunneling).
E[xwOBA | BIP] depends on pitch location, velocity/movement, and launch-angle suppression. Fitting dedicated logloss / RMSE heads to each physical transition prevents high-variance batted balls from drowning out sharp strike-zone and whiff boundaries.

Why Pitch-Level Zero-Mean Decision Value (Decision+) Beats Z-O%: Study 04’s Zone-Chase (Z-O%) treats every pitch inside the rulebook strike zone identically (+1) and every pitch outside identically (-1). In reality, swinging at a 3-0 fastball on the black is far less valuable than swinging at a 1-0 heart-zone meatball, and chasing a 3-2 slider (0.6018 run Ball-Strike spread!) is 8× costlier than chasing on 0-0 (0.0750 spread). Pricing each pitch’s exact \((\text{EV}_{\text{swing}} - \text{EV}_{\text{take}})\) and subtracting the league-average swing probability \(\hat{p}_{\text{sw}}\) yields a strictly zero-mean, pitch-mix-unbiased SEAGER-class metric.

title: Study 05: Context-Neutral Decomposed Pitching+ & Pitch-Level Batter Process Engine
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Zero-Leakage Architecture

3.1 Context-Neutral 12-Count Linear Weights & BIP xwOBA → RV Map (2015–2023 Train Only)
Strictly on 2015–2023 Regular-Season pitches (5,972,773 rows, zero 2024–2026 data), we compute empirical batter-perspective transition values for each count \((b, s) \in \{0..3\} \times \{0..2\}\): - \(\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{ball}}(b,s)\), \(\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}}(b,s)\), and \(\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{foul}}(b,s)\) (= 0.0000 identically when \(s = 2\)). - For balls in play (> 900K training BIPs with finite xwoba), OLS fits \(\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{BIP}}(b,s,\widehat{\text{xwOBA}}) = \alpha_{b,s} + \beta \cdot \widehat{\text{xwOBA}}\), yielding \(\beta = 0.8593\) (\(R^2 = 0.4472\), matching theoretical \(1 / w_{\text{scale}} \approx 0.86\) to three decimals!).


3.2 Five-Head Decomposed Expected Value & Martingale Count Centering
Given 5 chronological xgboost heads (\(\hat{p}_{\text{sw}}, \hat{p}_{\text{cs}}, \hat{p}_{\text{wh}}, \hat{p}_{\text{fl}}, \widehat{\text{xwOBA}}\)):
\[\text{EV}_{\text{take},i} = \hat{p}_{\text{cs},i}\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}}(b_i,s_i) + (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{cs},i})\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{ball}}(b_i,s_i)\] \[\text{EV}_{\text{contact},i} = \hat{p}_{\text{fl},i}\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{foul}}(b_i,s_i) + (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{fl},i})\big(\alpha_{b_i,s_i} + 0.8593\,\widehat{\text{xwOBA}}_i\big)\] \[\text{EV}_{\text{swing},i} = \hat{p}_{\text{wh},i}\,\Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}}(b_i,s_i) + (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{wh},i})\,\text{EV}_{\text{contact},i}\] \[\widehat{\text{xRV}}_{\text{bat},i} = (1 - \hat{p}_{\text{sw},i})\,\text{EV}_{\text{take},i} + \hat{p}_{\text{sw},i}\,\text{EV}_{\text{swing},i}\]

Count-Free Decomp Stuff+: Priced with marginal count-frequency-weighted linear weights (rv_ball = +0.0665, rv_strike = -0.1026), guaranteeing zero count or location leakage.
Martingale Count-Centered Location+ / Pitching+ / Pitching+Tunnel: Subtracting the 2020–2023 training mean within each count cell ensures \(\mathbb{E}[\text{xRV}_{\text{centered}} \mid b, s] \equiv 0\), so pitchers are graded purely on execution within each count.



3.3 Exact Additive Pitch-Level Batter Process Decomposition
Using the locked full-context Decomp Pitching+Tunnel probability surface:
\[\text{decision\_voe}_i = (I_{\text{swing},i} - \hat{p}_{\text{sw},i})\big(\text{EV}_{\text{swing},i} - \text{EV}_{\text{take},i}\big)\] \[\text{bat\_ctrl\_rv}_i = I_{\text{swing},i}\,(\hat{p}_{\text{wh},i} - I_{\text{whiff},i})\big(\text{EV}_{\text{contact},i} - \Delta\text{RV}_{\text{strike}}(b_i,s_i)\big)\] \[\text{contact\_rv}_i = I_{\text{bip},i} \cdot 0.8593 \cdot (\text{xwOBA}_i - \widehat{\text{xwOBA}}_i)\] \[\text{process\_rv}_i = \text{decision\_voe}_i + \text{bat\_ctrl\_rv}_i + \text{contact\_rv}_i\]
All season rates use sum-before-divide (rv100 = 100 * sum(rv) / n_pitches) and standardize to 100 ± 10 strictly on 2024 qualified cohorts (>= 500 pitches thrown; >= 1,000 pitches seen).

2. Domain Problem & Multi-Market Quantitative Structure
Sharp MLB syndicates separate pricing into distinct market horizons because signal-to-noise varies dramatically by inning: F5 Moneylines isolate starting pitcher physics (FIP + arm_angle ride), Full-Game Moneylines add dynamic 3-day bullpen exhaustion, Game Totals respond strongly to temperature/wind carry and home-plate umpire zone habits, and Championship Futures depend critically on MLB’s asymmetric 12-team bracket (where Top-2 division winners bypass the volatile Best-of-3 Wild Card round).

title: Pitch Type Classification with Random Forest
text:
Automated pitch classification models (such as MLB’s automated pitch tagging) use 3D kinematic tracking to predict the pitch type delivered by a pitcher. In this analysis, we train a multi-class Random Forest classifier via the tidymodels framework and the fast C++ ranger engine to predict six primary pitch types:

FF: Four-Seam Fastball
SI: Sinker / Two-Seam
SL: Slider
CH: Changeup
CU: Curveball
FC: Cutter

title: Pitch Type Classification with Random Forest
text:
Data Pipeline & Preprocessing
We query 25,000 right-handed pitches with complete physical parameters from the mlbr data lake via DuckDB:


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  .libPaths(c("/mnt/storage/R/library", .libPaths()))
  library(mlbr)
  library(duckdb)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidymodels)
  library(ranger)
  library(ggplot2)
})

con <- lake_duckdb()

df_pitches <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT 
    pitch_type,
    release_speed,
    release_spin_rate,
    pfx_x * 12.0 AS pfx_x_in,
    pfx_z * 12.0 AS pfx_z_in,
    vx0, vy0, vz0,
    ax, ay, az
  FROM statcast
  WHERE p_throws = 'R'
    AND pitch_type IN ('FF', 'SI', 'SL', 'CH', 'CU', 'FC')
    AND release_speed IS NOT NULL
    AND release_spin_rate IS NOT NULL
    AND pfx_x IS NOT NULL
    AND pfx_z IS NOT NULL
    AND vx0 IS NOT NULL
  USING SAMPLE 25000 (reservoir);
") %>%
  mutate(pitch_type = as.factor(pitch_type))

cat(sprintf("Prepared %d pitches for supervised classification.\n", nrow(df_pitches)))


Prepared 4098 pitches for supervised classification.

title: Pitch Type Classification with Random Forest
text:
Train / Test Splitting
We partition the dataset into an 80% training set and a 20% test holdout, stratified by pitch_type to preserve class proportions:


Code
set.seed(123)
pitch_split <- initial_split(df_pitches, prop = 0.80, strata = pitch_type)
train_data  <- training(pitch_split)
test_data   <- testing(pitch_split)

cat(sprintf("Training samples: %d | Test samples: %d\n", nrow(train_data), nrow(test_data)))


Training samples: 3276 | Test samples: 822

title: Pitch Type Classification with Random Forest
text:
Model Specification & Training
We specify a Random Forest classifier with 200 decision trees, capturing non-linear interactions between velocity, spin, and aerodynamic acceleration vectors:


Code
rf_spec <- rand_forest(trees = 200, mode = "classification") %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity", num.threads = 8)

pitch_recipe <- recipe(pitch_type ~ ., data = train_data)

rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(pitch_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)

# Fit workflow on training set
cat("Training Random Forest model on 8 threads...\n")


Training Random Forest model on 8 threads...


Code
rf_fit <- fit(rf_workflow, data = train_data)

title: Pitch Type Classification with Random Forest

We evaluate model predictions against the unseen holdout test set:


Code
test_preds <- predict(rf_fit, test_data) %>%
  bind_cols(predict(rf_fit, test_data, type = "prob")) %>%
  bind_cols(test_data %>% select(pitch_type))

# Compute Accuracy and Macro ROC-AUC
acc_res <- accuracy(test_preds, truth = pitch_type, estimate = .pred_class)
roc_res <- roc_auc(test_preds, truth = pitch_type, .pred_CH:.pred_SL)

metrics_df <- bind_rows(acc_res, roc_res)

title: Study 18: Same-Game Parlay (SGP) Correlation Matrix & Gaussian/Clayton Copula Pricing Engine
text:
1. Executive Summary & Abstract (TL;DR)
Combining multiple wagers from the same MLB contest into a Same-Game Parlay (SGP) invalidates naive independence multiplication (\(P(A \cap B) \ne p_A p_B\)) because every leg shares the same realization of game physics, plate appearances, and run scoring. In EXP-018, we join all six previously validated mlbr market engines (Full-Game ML, F5 ML, Game Totals Over 8.5, NegBin SP Strikeout Props, Batter HR 1+, and Batter TB 2+) across 4,859 regular-season games (87,462 starting batter-games), fit Gaussian and Clayton (including 90°-rotated) copulas strictly via 2024 bivariate Bernoulli MLE, and evaluate strictly out-of-sample on locked 2025:

Massive Naive Independence Mispricing Exposed: Across Home ML + F5 Home Win (\(\hat{\rho}_{2024} = +0.839\)), naive independence underprices the parlay by -18.0 percentage points (27.6% vs 45.6% actual). Our Gaussian Copula applies a 1.56x fair-price multiplier, slashing locked 2025 Parlay Log-Loss from 0.756 \(\to\) 0.680 (Brier 0.275 \(\to\) 0.243).
Batter-Game & Batter-Total Scripts (n = 43,740 OOS): On Batter HR 1+ + Team ML (\(\hat{\rho}_{2024} = +0.228\), 1.29x multiplier), copula pricing collapses calibration bias from -2.04 pp to -0.38 pp (Log-Loss 0.268 \(\to\) 0.265). On Batter TB 2+ + Game Over 8.5 (\(\hat{\rho}_{2024} = +0.245\), 1.23x multiplier), Clayton Copula cuts bias from -5.04 pp to -1.40 pp (Log-Loss 0.521 \(\to\) 0.512).
3-Leg Multivariate Gaussian Copula (n = 21,870 OOS): On Home ML + Home Batter TB 2+ + Game Over 8.5, exact 3D Gaussian Copula integration (1.36x multiplier) cuts absolute pricing bias by 80.2% (-3.81 pp \(\to\) -0.76 pp) and reduces Log-Loss from 0.378 \(\to\) 0.369.
Gaussian vs. Clayton Verdict: Both families deliver near-identical OOS accuracy on 2-leg MLB SGPs, while the Gaussian Copula generalizes natively to arbitrary \(d\)-leg correlation matrices (\(\mathbf{R} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\)) with exact Fréchet-Hoeffding compliance.




MLB Same-Game Parlay Empirical Market Correlation Matrix

title: Study 18: Same-Game Parlay (SGP) Correlation Matrix & Gaussian/Clayton Copula Pricing Engine
text:
2. Domain Problem & Within-Game Dependence Mechanics
Every MLB contest is a coupled stochastic process where single atomic events simultaneously move multiple betting markets:

Positive Script Coupling (\(\rho > 0\)): A starting batter hitting a home run (HR >= 1) directly adds 1–4 runs to his club’s score, boosting both his team’s win probability (Team ML) and the game total (Over 8.5). Similarly, leading after 5 innings (F5 Home Win) locks in a multi-run advantage entering the late innings (Home ML, \(\hat{\rho} = +0.839\)).
Negative Adversary Coupling (\(\rho < 0\)): When a starting pitcher dominates (Home SP Over 5.5 K), he suppresses opposing baserunners and reduces total scoring (Game Over 8.5, \(\hat{\rho} = -0.191\)). Likewise, when a batter erupts for TB >= 2, the opposing starter faces higher pitch counts and earlier hooks (Opp SP Over 5.5 K, \(\hat{\rho} = -0.118\)).
Marginal Drift vs. Copula Dependence: Evaluating only the single joint cell \(P_{11}\) can be confounded by year-over-year marginal base-rate drift (e.g., 2025 starter K rates shifted slightly above 2024 priors). Evaluating the full 4-cell Joint Log-Likelihood over \((00, 01, 10, 11)\) isolates pure dependence fidelity: on Home SP O5.5 K + Game Over 8.5, both copulas strictly improve 4-cell Joint NLL (1.31 \(\to\) 1.30) even under marginal drift.

title: Study 18: Same-Game Parlay (SGP) Correlation Matrix & Gaussian/Clayton Copula Pricing Engine
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Lake-Wide Pipeline
By Sklar’s Theorem (1959), given pre-game marginal probabilities \((p_1, \dots, p_d) \in (0,1)^d\) from EXP-014, EXP-016, and EXP-017, the joint SGP hit probability is:
\[P(Y_1 = 1, \dots, Y_d = 1) = C(p_1, \dots, p_d; \boldsymbol{\psi})\]
strictly bounded by the Fréchet-Hoeffding limits \(\max(0, \sum p_j - (d-1)) \le C \le \min(p_j)\).

Exact Vectorized Copulas

Bivariate Gaussian Copula (Plackett 1954 Integral via 16-Point Gauss-Legendre): \[C_{\text{Gauss}}(u, v; \rho) = uv + \int_0^\rho \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{1 - r^2}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{z_1^2 - 2 r z_1 z_2 + z_2^2}{2(1 - r^2)}\right)dr, \quad z_1 = \Phi^{-1}(u),\; z_2 = \Phi^{-1}(v)\] Verified against mvtnorm::pmvnorm to \(< 10^{-6}\) while running in < 10 ms across 43,740 batter-games.
Clayton Copula (Lower-Tail Exceedance for \(\rho \ge 0\), 90°-Rotated for \(\rho < 0\)): \[C_{\theta}^{\text{Cl}}(u, v) = \left(u^{-\theta} + v^{-\theta} - 1\right)^{-1/\theta}, \qquad C_{\theta}^{90^\circ}(u, v) = v - C_{\theta}^{\text{Cl}}(1 - u, v)\]
3D Multivariate Gaussian Copula: Exact 1D conditional reduction integrating \(\Phi_2(\cdot \mid Z_1)\) over \(Z_1 \le \Phi^{-1}(u_1)\), verified against 3D mvtnorm::pmvnorm (max diff = 1.26e-5).

-- Zero-copy DuckDB join uniting all 6 validated mlbr market engines
SELECT g.game_id, g.season, g.home_win, g.f5_home_win,
       CASE WHEN g.actual_total_runs >= 9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS y_over85,
       g.p_m6_ml, g.p_m6_f5, g.exp_total_m6,
       kh.y_over_5_5 AS y_hsp_o55, kh.p_m4_o55 AS p_hsp_o55,
       ka.y_over_5_5 AS y_asp_o55, ka.p_m4_o55 AS p_asp_o55
FROM read_parquet('data/processed/unified_pro_game_f5_totals_2024_2025.parquet') g
LEFT JOIN read_parquet('data/processed/dynamic_statespace_negbin_kprops_2024_2025.parquet') kh
  ON g.game_id = kh.game_id AND kh.is_home_sp = 1
LEFT JOIN read_parquet('data/processed/dynamic_statespace_negbin_kprops_2024_2025.parquet') ka
  ON g.game_id = ka.game_id AND ka.is_home_sp = 0;

7. Downstream Integration & Market Applications

Sportsbook SGP Hold Auditing: Retail sportsbooks routinely charge 15%–30% effective hold on 2-leg and 3-leg SGPs by over-penalizing positive correlations (Home ML + Batter HR) while offering little or no discount on negative correlations (SP O5.5 K + Game Over 8.5). Comparing offered SGP decimal odds \(O_{\text{book}}\) against \(1 / P_{\text{Gauss}}(A \cap B)\) immediately surfaces true fair-value edge and hidden vig.
Portfolio Risk Management (EXP-010 Integration): The same latent correlation matrix \(\hat{\mathbf{R}}\) governs simultaneous same-game bets placed across separate single-game markets (e.g., betting both Home ML and Home SP O5.5 K), enabling covariance-adjusted multivariate Kelly sizing rather than assuming independent tickets.

2. Domain Problem & Batter Prop Mechanics
Batter Home Run and Total Bases props are driven by a multiplicative stack of 5 pre-game observables: (1) true-talent swing energy (bat_speed, Blast Rate, ISO), (2) PA exposure via batting-order slot (#1–#4 average ~0.7 more PAs per game than #9), (3) platoon advantage vs. the opposing starter’s handedness, (4) handedness-specific venue geometry (pf_hr_lhb vs. pf_hr_rhb), and (5) game-time aerodynamic carry (temp_f and Chadwick wind_out_mph).
crumbs: Study 17: Batter HR & Total Bases Props

title: Study 17: Batter Home Run (HR >= 1) & Total Bases (TB >= 2) Prop Pricing Engine
text:
3. Mathematical Formulation & Native Lake Pipeline
\[\text{logit}\big(P(\text{HR}_i \ge 1)\big) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{ISO}_{t-1}^{\text{EB}} + \beta_2 \text{HR\%}_{t-1}^{\text{EB}} + \beta_3 \text{BatSpeed}_{t-1} + \beta_4 \text{Blast}_{t-1} + \beta_5 \text{Slot}_i + \beta_6 \text{Platoon}_i + \beta_7 \text{PF}_{\text{HR,hand}} + \beta_8 \text{Temp}_F + \beta_9 \text{WindOut} + \beta_{10} \text{OppSP\_HR\%}_{t-1}\]
SET memory_limit = '12GB';
SELECT game_year, COUNT(*) AS n_pitches, SUM(is_blast) AS n_blasts,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN bat_speed_dbl >= 60 THEN bat_speed_dbl END), 2) AS mean_bs
FROM v_statcast_biomechanics
WHERE game_year >= 2023
GROUP BY game_year ORDER BY game_year;

7. Downstream Integration & Market Applications
With 17 completed, audited Q-CRISP studies (EXP-001–EXP-017), 17 native zero-copy DuckDB views, and 17 companion RStudio labs, mlbr now prices six distinct MLB quantitative markets end-to-end strictly out-of-sample: Full-Game ML, F5 ML, Over/Under Totals, Pitcher Strikeout Props (NegBin State-Space), Batter HR & Total Bases Props, and Exact 12-Team Playoff & World Series Futures.
